title: Penn State football vs Marshall time, TV, odds, storylines
description: Everything you need to know for Penn State football vs Marshall, including kickoff time, TV channel, injury updates, betting odds, and predictions.
fullText:
A new Penn State football era begins on the field Saturday afternoon in Beaver Stadium.

Head coach Matt Campbell and his new staff and overhauled Nittany Lion roster will open their 2026 season against the Marshall Thundering Herd. These new-look Lions, which ended last season with four-straight wins, return only a handful of starters.

Whether you're looking for kickoff information, injury updates, betting odds, key matchups or score predictions, this guide has everything you need to know before the Lions play for the first time under Campbell.

Like these bold predictions for the upcoming season ...

We'll update this story throughout the week with the latest injury news, coach comments and game-day developments leading up to kickoff.

Streaming: Fubo (with a free trial)

The Nittany Lions open their 2026 season at 3:30 p.m. on Sept. 5 against Marshall in Beaver Stadium.

Penn State vs. Marshall will be aired on FS1 (FOX Sports 1).

The game can be streamed live on FUBO (with a free trial).

Penn State -3000; Marshall +1500

All eyes will be on the overhauled Penn State offense with the strong Iowa State flavor − from hopeful star quarterback Rocco Becht to tailback Carson Hansen to All-America candidate tight end Ben Brahmer to another wait-and-see receiver room.

How quickly, smoothly will this group produce against a prohibitive underdog − a Marshall team coming off a losing season with serious issues on defense?

Becht's work with that receiver group, which includes a few intriguing freshmen, will be at the forefront first.

title: San Jose State head coach Ken Niumatalolo praises USC after loss
description: The Trojans earned the respect of San Jose State’s head coach in their victory over the Spartans on Saturday
fullText:
On Saturday, USC opened up its 2026 season by handling San Jose State 42-26 at the Coliseum. With the victory, the Trojans started off the year 1-0.

In his press conference following the game, San Jose State head coach Ken Niumatalolo praised the Trojans.

"Well, first off, hats off to USC and Coach [Lincoln] Riley," Niumatalolo said. "That's a really great football team. We struggled all day trying to find a way to stop them. When you can run the ball like they were doing early on in the game, gaining six yards of play. It makes it tough to play defense. They kind of had the same quality there just because of the run game, big physical line, and a super elusive physical runner. So it kind of had us on our heels a little bit defensively."

In particular, Niumatalolo had extremely positive things to say about USC defensive coordinator Gary Patterson.

"I know Gary Patterson very well," Niumatalolo said. "Smart call by Lincoln to hire him. They're going to get people in trouble in the Big Ten, and that's just their first game. And as they grow, they're going to get better with Gary leading their defense. But Gary's a phenomenal football coach. He's a phenomenal culture builder, and a credit to Lincoln. To have the humility as a head coach, and the foresight to hire a Hall-of-Famer. A lot of coaches wouldn't do that. They're like, 'No, I'm not going to hire a guy that caliber in my chair.' But to his credit, Lincoln hired a guy that's one of the best defensive minds of all time."

While Riley and USC started off the season 1-0 with the victory, Niumatalolo and San Jose State fell to 0-1. The Spartans will visit Eastern Michigan next week.

title: An Optimist’s Guide for the 2026 Football Season.
description: 2026 is the year of the Hawk
fullText:
Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No! It's Iowa pass catchers flying through the air. There is so much to love about the upcoming 2026 campaign for the Hawks. Iowa has been flying so far under the radar (thank you, Kyle Whittingham) that it can't help but make you feel like Odysseus in that wooden horse. Kirk Ferentz is Matt Damon trying to get his Hawkeyes back to national glory. It took Damon 20 years, and Kirk is trying to get back to the heights reached in 2010. Does Kirk have the horses to pull off an epic conclusion to an immaculate career? I absolutely believe in the 2026 Hawks' chances to sneak their way to their first playoff berth.

#Michigan HC Kyle Whittingham on his comments about not hating Ohio State from Big Ten media days: 

“Do we have a better chance of winning if I hated them? I don’t understand. Whatever gives us the best chance to win, I’m all for it. I want to beat them worst than anybody.” pic.twitter.com/e4fjLPBltT

Let me be absolutely clear: there's a plethora of things that need to go Iowa's way for there to be a shot at making the big dance. It really comes down to the development of the younger guys coming to fruition. All Hawk fans hear about is development, which can be scary after an offseason. On paper, this is a 7- or 8-win team, but it feels like we have some flowers to bloom fully. There are some guys I'm buying all the available stock on this year that will boom in a gargantuan way.

The non-negotiable, most crucial domino to fall is Jeremy Hecklinski beating out Hank Brown and staying healthy. I have nothing against Hanky Ballgame, but the talent Hecklinski possesses is intoxicating. Hecklinski is Moxie personified. He has a personality that gives me more hope than the more laid-back personality of Brown. The concern about Hecklinski's size is certainly valid. I stood next to the guy at an establishment that rhymes with Mothers in Iowa City, and yikes.

I stand at 5 feet 9 inches on a great day, and I was eye to eye with Hecklinski. Not the best feeling when your quarterback is the same size as you. He's 1 million times more athletic than me, who is currently sipping on a sea salt caramel Cold brew right now (so delicious). For the record, I usually roll with straight black coffee, but I caved.

Despite the size concerns, Hecklinski put on a clinic at Kids Day at Kinnick. Hecklinski went 17-for-25 for 205 yards, 5 touchdowns, and 0 picks, according to David Eickholt. After watching the tape, it's an even more impressive stat line because those incompletions were mostly really good decisions to avoid a negative play. Hecklinski is avoiding big hits and getting the ball to his skill players, which will be key in getting the Hawks to where they need to go.

FILM: Here's every Jeremy Hecklinski drop back we captured at Iowa's Kids' Day scrimmage. pic.twitter.com/LeJtZBlTjB

In all seriousness, there is going to be a lot of weight placed on whoever wins out of fall camp. Pressure is a privilege, especially for the 26 season. Whoever wins out will have the deepest arsenal of weapons an Iowa quarterback has seen since COVID. For as bad as Cade McNamara was, the skill positions might have been equally as weak.

There was a time we were so desperate for dynamism, we threw Cooper Dejean on offense for a few snaps. I love Dejean as much as the next guy, but that was an indicator of a dark time for Iowa's offense. I feel really good about the 7 pass catchers the Hawks can throw out there. SEVEN WEAPONS! A few years ago, it was unthinkable we could recover from the BF disaster.

The tight ends are spectacular. DJ Vonnahme is going to win the Mackey Award this year. I do not doubt that what I saw against Vanderbilt (146 yards) was the anointing of the next great Iowa tight end. If Vonnohme doesn't win the Mackey, I'd at least pencil him in for making an All-American team. What separates this TE room from past ones is that we have four starting-caliber guys that will all see the field this year. Talking about the TE's is burying the lead of what is different from past Hawkeye squads.

There's a chance I have died, and I'm living in a dream-like state where Iowa has fixed the wide receiver position. Brian Ferentz did everything he could to ruin the reputation of the Iowa offense.

Side note: it bugs the crap out of me that his stink still lingers around Iowa. National talking heads and casual social media CFB fans will still make jokes about Iowa not being able to score. Hahahhaha, it's hilarious, @CFBLover11! It's so true that Iowa can't score. Whatever. It's the fastest way to expose yourself as a fraud of a college football fan.

Iowa announces 1847 Bourbon & 1847 Vodka as school’s official bourbon & vodka partners. Each bottle features a co-branded design w/iconic Tigerhawk logo. Fans are required to take a shot after every punt, safety or defensive TD

Luckily, players have taken notice of the marvelous turnaround Iowa has made. Frankly, I'm still baffled that Tony Diaz, a WR transfer from UTRGV, chose the Hawks over Alabama. Somebody pinch me! All the reports indicate that Tony Diaz is the freak athlete he was billed to be. Diaz is paired with Vander Zee, who is a jump ball demon that complements Diaz's skill set. Throwing in towering Dayton Howard and the quick Evan James to do impressions of the top guys is promising.

1️⃣0️⃣👉1️⃣4️⃣ pic.twitter.com/42eB1LYoFF

On the other side of the ball, It's Phil Parker we trust. This won't be the most stacked Iowa defense of the past 10 years, but it will be right in the middle of the pack. The defense has an interesting mix of veterans and young talents who are ready to perform. Zach Lutmer, Jayden Montgomery, and Deshaun Lee will be back to usher in the next era of Iowa defense. On the defensive line, the Hawks should be greatly improved. The lack of a pass rush was addressed in the transfer portal, bringing in Khamri Brown from Elon.

You can roll your eyes at Elon, but Brown is a gifted athlete. Racking up 12 sacks in 2025 earned Brown a spot on Bruce Feldman's annual freaks list. When you go on the opposite side of the freak, you have Iose Epesnesa. I haven't been this excited since they brought back the snack wrap at McDonald's. Iose's big bro brought me so much joy in my life; I smile at the fact that we'll get to see that last name rush the passer again. A better pass rush should help all levels that should be at the same level is not better than last year.

True freshman Marcello Vitti is a name that has generated a ton of buzz in both spring and fall camp. Vitti could be the rare true freshman that makes a big impact on defense. Definitely something to monitor when entering the season.

All the aforementioned optimism pales in comparison to the real reason the Hawks will make their first playoff berth. It's Tim MFing Lester.

The offense has improved exponentially since he arrived in 2024, and there are no signs of slowing down growth in 2026. Lester finally has the guys he needs to complete his masterpiece of a rebuild. I love Mark Gronowski with my whole heart, but he was a bridge. Gronowski was a vital bridge; don't get me wrong, but he wasn't the destination. The destination is a complex system of quick passing and decision-making. Hecklinski looked as smooth as a Husker fan's brain on Kids Day.

A lot of the time, simply getting it out quickly will be all that is asked. The playmakers are finally a strength, and Tim Lester knows that. Getting the ball to the fast and strong guys as quickly as possible seems to be the name of the game. The system is going to hum to the likes we haven't seen in a decade. Watch out, Big Ten: Iowa has an excellent offensive attack.

A TE tradition in Kinnick.@JHecklinski ➡️ @dj_vonnahme pic.twitter.com/iQ7btbcItH

There's no reason you- yes, you- shouldn't be thinking playoffs. It's right there for the taking. Win ⅔ of @Washington, Vs Ohio State, @Michigan, and we're staring at the big dance. Get vocal at your water cooler and let your annoying Michigan grad coworker know that we're coming for blood in the Big House. It's time to throw cautious optimism out the window.

Life is about experiencing big feelings and making momentous memories that shape our experience. Lift your walls and let both the waves of agony and elation wash over you. Why be cautious in your belief? Be belligerently hopeful that 2026 is the year of the Hawkeyes.

title: Pukstas joins US contingent at Middlesbrough
description: Rokas Pukstas becomes the third American to sign for Middlesbrough this season following his arrival from Hajduk Split.
fullText:
Middlesbrough have signed their third American player this summer with the arrival of midfielder Rokas Pukstas for a fee reported to be about £4.3m (5m euros).

The 22-year-old has joined Boro from Croatian club Hadjuk Split on a five-year contract and is their 10th senior recruit in the transfer window.

Pukstas joins midfield compatriot Sebastian Berhalter and winger Max Arfsten at the Riverside, where they have linked up with fellow American Aidan Morris who was already in the squad.

Pukstas, who is of Lithuanian descent, has spent his entire professional career in Croatia but has played for the US age-group teams up to Under-23 level.

"I had a call with the coach and directors here," he told the Middlesbrough website.

"He (Kim Hellberg) is a fascinating coach, the people are lovely and it reminds me of home. Everything seems aligned now I'm here."

Boro are fifth in the Championship with two wins from their opening three matches.

title: Puck Drop Preview: 2026-27 Chicago Blackhawks
description: Last Word On Hockey‘s Puck Drop Previews are back for the 2026-27 season! As the regular season approaches, Last Word will preview each team’s current outlook and stories to watch for the upcoming year. We’ll also do our best to project how things will go for each team throughout the campaign. Today, we’re previewing the 2026-27 …
fullText:
Last Word On Hockey's Puck Drop Previews are back for the 2026-27 season! As the regular season approaches, Last Word will preview each team's current outlook and stories to watch for the upcoming year. We'll also do our best to project how things will go for each team throughout the campaign. Today, we're previewing the 2026-27 Chicago Blackhawks.

The 2025-26 season marked the sixth-consecutive season that the Blackhawks missed the Stanley Cup Playoffs. It really is not at all surprising. The Blackhawks are still trying to rebuild around phenom Connor Bedard. With a record of 29-39-14, the Blackhawks finished with 72 points, last in the Central Division and second-to-last in the entire league. This set them up for a solid position to either draft first or second in the 2026 NHL Entry Draft. Unfortunately for the Blackhawks, they ended up moving back two positions, earning the fourth-overall selection in the draft.

The 2026 offseason got started off with a bang for the Blackhawks. After the Blackhawks lost the draft lottery and earned the right to draft fourth overall, general manager Kyle Davidson elected to trade the pick to the Buffalo Sabres along with the 45th-overall selection and Louis Crevier in exchange for Bowen Byram and Jordan Greenway. This was a major move for the Blackhawks, who are trying to take the next step in their rebuild by bringing in some more proven talent to play around Bedard, Frank Nazar and Anton Frondell. After trading for Byram, the club signed him to a six-year deal worth $75 million, carrying an average annual value of $12.5 million per season.

The next major move saw the Blackhawks bring back future Hall of Famer Patrick Kane on a two-year deal worth $16 million. This will be Kane's second stint with the club after they originally drafted him first overall in the 2007 NHL Draft. Kane helped the Blackhawks win three Stanley Cups during his first tenure and is hoping to help lead the Blackhawks back to the Playoffs in his return.

The offseason has certainly been one of improvement for the Blackhawks as they look to end their six-year playoff skid.

Extras:  Cole Smith, Nick Lardis

Though Connor Bedard is going to miss at least the first month of the regular season, the newly formed top-six is filled with offensive firepower. Kane joining the fold to play alongside Bedard could produce one of the most exciting duos in the entire league this season. Match that with highly touted prospect Roman Kantserov coming over from the KHL after leading the league in goals last season, the Blackhawks top line should be extremely fun to watch.

The second line of Nazar, Bertuzzi, and Frondell should also be an exciting trio in their own right. Frondell made the jump to the NHL last season, scoring three goals and nine assists in 12 games as a 19-year-old. Nazar upped his production from his rookie season by producing 15 goals and 41 points in 66 games. Add an agitating, high-energy power forward like Bertuzzi to the mix, and the Blackhawks have created a very respectable top-six capable of producing goals. Something they really struggled to do last season.

The bottom six will feature a strong mix of NHL veterans with a couple of young, promising prospects. Much like Kane, Teravainen is enduring his second stint with the Blackhawks. He's entering his third season with the Blackhawks since signing with them prior to the 2024-25 season. Teravainen won a Stanley Cup with Kane during the 2014-15 season and is hoping to help turn things around for the club this upcoming season.

Joining him will be Jordan Greenway, who came over in a trade from the Buffalo Sabres and brings some much-needed grit to the lineup. As well as promising young players like Ryan Greene and Oliver Moore. Greene played his first full season with the Blackhawks last season, scoring 12 goals and adding 17 assists in 81 games. For his part in his first season, Moore scored five goals and 14 assists in 51 games. The high-energy forward plays a solid 200-foot game and possesses high hockey IQ and has the versatility to play both centre and the wing. Something that will prove extremely valuable as he continues to develop for the Blackhawks.

The top four for the Blackhawks will feature the newly acquired Bowen Byram leading the way on the top pair, as well as top defence prospect Artyom Levshunov. Byram will likely be paired with the steady giant Alex Vlasic, while the former second-overall selection Levshunov will be paired with fellow youngster Wyatt Kaiser. This top four should prove to be very steady for the Blackhawks and should be locked in as the top four group for years to come.

The bottom pair is a bit interesting. This pairing will likely change quite a bit with Kevin Korchinski coming in and out of the lineup for one of Cole or Rinzel. The newly signed Korchinski will be an interesting piece for the group as he is no longer eligible for waivers. The 22-year-old entered the league as a 19-year-old. However, he hasn't really developed into the defenceman the Blackhawks thought they were drafting when they selected him seventh overall back in 2022. He will certainly push hard for an everyday place in the Blackhawks lineup this season after earning a prove-it deal just a couple of days ago. The Blackhawks definitely will want to keep him up with the roster as well, as they would certainly lose him on waivers if they elected to place him there.

Spencer Knight returns as the club's starting goaltender for the 2026-27 season and will look to build off a solid first season starting for the Blackhawks. Playing in front of a very young Blackhawks group, Knight showed why he was drafted 13th overall in the 2019 NHL Entry Draft, posting 19-25-11 record with a 2.82 goals-against average and a .902 save percentage. With a much-improved Blackhawks team entering the 2026-27 season, Knight should have every chance to surpass those numbers from last season.

Knight will be the workhorse for the team, as Soderblom will likely play in fewer than 30 games for the team. Soderblom has never produced a save percentage above .900 or a goals-against average under 3.00. Though he has played on some dismal Blackhawks teams, expect the club to turn to Knight on most nights.

The newly acquired Byram will have his first chance to be the leader of a defence group this season with the Blackhawks. The Blackhawks have high expectations for the young defender after dealing the fourth, 45th, and Crevier for him this offseason, then signing him for $12.5 million per season. Despite the pressure of the new contract on a very young Blackhawks team, the 25-year-old defender has all the tools to earn every dollar of his contract, and should be able to accomplish new highs in goals and points again this season, after having a career year with the Sabres which saw him score 11 goals and 42 points in 82 games.

Nazar had a very productive 2025-26 season, scoring 15 goals and 41 points in 66 games. The 13th-overall selection in the 2022 NHL Entry Draft will have every opportunity to grow on that as he will be expected to line up as the clubs number one centre, at least until Bedard returns from injury.

The 2026-27 Chicago Blackhawks are a much-improved group who will certainly take the next step in their rebuild. Led by Bedard and Kane, the Blackhawks will improve their goal scoring from the second-to-last position they finished last season. Youngsters Frondell, Moore, Greene, Levshunov, and Kantserov will bring some added excitement to the lineup and should be able to cement themselves as staples in the lineup for years to come. Spencer Knight will continue to build on his excellent first season as a starter for the Blackhawks and prove that he will be their starter for the foreseeable future. Despite all this, the Blackhawks will once again miss the Stanley Cup Playoffs. They will inch closer and play some more meaningful games down the stretch; however, they will ultimately still be on the outside looking in.

title: Mateu Morey joins Girona FC until June 2028
description: Girona FC signs Mateu Morey. The right-back, who joins from RCD Mallorca, has signed with the Club for the next two seasons and will wear the red-and-white jersey until June 2028.Born in Petra (Mallor...
fullText:
Girona FC signs Mateu Morey. The right-back, who joins from RCD Mallorca, has signed with the Club for the next two seasons and will wear the red-and-white jersey until June 2028.

Born in Petra (Mallorca) on March 2, 2000, Morey is a well-rounded right-back, capable of also playing in more advanced positions. He stands out for his physical strength, speed, defensive ability, and intensity in duels, as well as his capacity to join the attack and reach the final third. His profile allows him to contribute both in the defensive phase and in ball progression and distribution.

Initially trained in Mallorca's youth academy, Morey later moved through the youth ranks of FC Barcelona, where he was part of the youth team that won the 2017/18 UEFA Youth League. During the same period, he also represented Spain at the U-17 level and participated in winning the 2017 U-17 European Championship, playing in 7 matches. He later joined Borussia Dortmund, a club where he completed much of his development and made the leap to professional football.

With the German team, he played 32 matches with the first team, as well as 18 with Borussia Dortmund II, and was part of the squad that won the 2019 German Super Cup and the 2021 German Cup.

In the summer of 2024, he returned to his original club, RCD Mallorca, where he played for the last two seasons. During this period, he accumulated 38 official matches and scored one goal with Mallorca's first team. In the 2025/26 season, he participated in 21 matches, 18 of which were in LaLiga, and scored one goal.

Morey now arrives in Girona at the age of 26 with extensive experience in elite football, having competed in LaLiga, Bundesliga, Copa del Rey, German Cup, and UEFA Champions League. Internationally, he has also represented Spain at the U-17 and U-21 levels.

With this signing, Girona FC adds to its project a right-back with international experience, physical ability, and a proven track record in professional football.

title: St Kilda give McDonald permission for GAA return
description: All-Ireland winner Kobe McDonald will return to Gaelic football for the Mayo Senior Football Championship after being granted permission by AFL side St Kilda.
fullText:
All-Ireland winner Kobe McDonald will return to Gaelic football for Crossmolina in the Mayo Senior Football Championship after being granted permission by AFL side St Kilda.

St Kilda had previously allowed the 18-year-old to play for Mayo as they ended their 75-year wait to win the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship in July.

McDonald, who only made his Mayo debut in February, played a key role in the final win over Kerry, and was set to move to Melbourne to start his Aussie Rules career following that success.

But with St Kilda's season over and pre-season in the AFL not starting until November, McDonald, Eamonn Armstrong and Liam O'Connell have been granted permission to return to their club sides for their respective championships.

Armstrong plays for Duleek Bellewstown in the Meath championship, while O'Connell, who featured 13 times for St Kilda's in the AFL last season, is set to line out for Ballincollig in the Cork SFC.

McDonald has been in Ireland over the past number of weeks, and was pictured with the Mayo squad on stage with the Saw Doctors at the Electric Picnic festival in Laois on Sunday.

Lenny Hayes, St Kilda's general manager of football, said the trio had "expressed a desire" to play for their clubs.

"As a club, it's really important that we support our players in their lives outside of being professional AFL footballers," Hayes told the Irish Examiner.

"We understand how much home means to each of these boys, and we didn't want to stand in the way of this opportunity to represent the communities and clubs they come from.

"The opportunity to play should only benefit their aerobic conditioning, and we look forward to welcoming them back in November for the first day of pre-season."

title: Arsenal slash wage bill as Martinelli to Al-Hilal and Jesus to Barcelona take summer salary savings to £893k
description: Arsenal are have cut almost £1m per week from their wage bill this summer after trimming the squad.The North Londoners have sought to offload several fringe players during the current window, with Ga...
fullText:
Arsenal are have cut almost £1m per week from their wage bill this summer after trimming the squad.

The North Londoners have sought to offload several fringe players during the current window, with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus the latest pair set to leave the Emirates.

Martinelli is nearing a club-record sale to Al-Hilal, with the Saudi Pro League side have agreed a fee of around £55m with Arsenal. Jesus is also close to finalising a cut-price move to Barcelona, in deals that will see Arsenal's saving on wages reach £893,000-a-week.

Jesus offers the biggest saving, having earned £265,000-a-week in North London, despite falling out of favour. The Brazilian's wages were the third-highest in the Arsenal squad, behind Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz.

Martinelli's £180,000-a-week wages are also soon to be off the books. Elsewhere, Arsenal have saved further from the sales of Leandro Trossard (£180,000-a-week), Fabio Vieira (£45,000-a-week, Jakub Kiwior (£58,000-a-week), Christian Norgaard (£65,000-a-week) and the release of Reiss Nelson (£100,000-a-week).

Arsenal have reinvested around £530,000-a-week in the wages of Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa, Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier, but with £363,000-a-week saved, could a late marquee addition still be on the agenda?

title: Norwich City 4-1 Burnley - fans' verdict
description: We asked for your thoughts after Saturday's Championship match between Norwich City and Burnley.
fullText:
We asked for your thoughts after Saturday's Championship match between Norwich City and Burnley.

Here are some of your comments:

Canary Kid: Much better. Oddly enough, perhaps it comes with following Norwich, I wasn't feeling comfortable, even at 3-0. Burnley, very impressive going forward. They won't be winless for long.

Mark: As much as I was happy with the 4-1 score line, if Burnley had scored (rather than hit the post) at the start of the second half and made it 3-2, it would've been interesting to see how Norwich would've reacted to that.

However, the fast start (two up in five minutes) shocked Burnley and they never really recovered despite getting into the odd good attacking position. Top eight definitely possible if we keep our squad healthy. OTBC.

Keith: That's better - hope Canaries will keep it up. Up The City!

Andy: Shambles in defence and weak in midfield. Satpaev the only real positive in a team struggling for confidence. Edwards shouldn't be on the pitch until he gets his desire back - no commitment or energy. The manager needs to pick a side capable of competing and battling for the club. Too many players not giving 100%.

Anthony: I expected Norwich to brush us aside, but not in the first five minutes, after which the game was over as a contest.

No leadership in the club, both on and off the pitch and with many players who simply don't show any desire to stay or play, but just to see out lengthy, lucrative contracts. Achieving 50 points by the season end is no more than a dream.

Graeme: Utterly abysmal. 60% of the possession and unable to do anything with it. Already in the relegation zone and absolutely no confidence that these players are capable of getting out of it.

What do they do in training? The "forwards" obviously don't practice hitting the target. Desperately need several experienced strikers and preferably some decent defenders as well. Otherwise, it's hopeless.

Marquee summer signing Rodri is included again and might make his first start as a Barcelona player.

Meanwhile, fellow midfielder Frenkie de Jong is a long-term absentee for the Catalans, along with Roony Bardghji.

title: Official: Inter send Massolin to Cagliari in potential €7m deal with buy-back option

fullText:
Cagliari have officially announced their signing of 23-year-old talent Yanis Massolin on loan with an option to buy from Inter, who will retain a buy-back option in the event that the transfer is made permanent.

"Cagliari is pleased to announce the acquisition of the sporting rights to the footballer Yanis Massolin, who joins the Rossobluu from Inter on loan until the end of the 2026-27 season with an option to buy and a buy-back option," confirmed a statement on the club website.

According to reports from Fabrizio Romano, Cagliari will have to pay a fee of €7m to purchase Massolin on a definitive basis. Inter had paid a fee of €8m including bonuses and add-ons to sign the youngster from Modena in the winter transfer window earlier this year.

Yanis Massolin joins Innter from Modena

Massolin has not yet appeared competitively for the Nerazzurri, as he immediately returned to Modena on a six-month loan deal after moving to San Siro at the end of the January transfer window.

The attacking midfielder provided three goals and three assists from 28 appearances in Serie B during the 2025-26 season.

The 2026-27 season will bring his first experience in the Italian top flight. He also has spells with Francs Borains and Clermont on his CV.

title: Cheslin Kolbe given new role as Springboks suffer injury blow ahead of third Test against New Zealand
description: Kolbe will start at full-back at FNB Stadium with Damian Willemse ruled out through injury
fullText:
Cheslin Kolbe will start at full-back with Damian Willemse ruled out of South Africa's third Test clash with New Zealand.

Kolbe relocates from the wing with Kurt-Lee Arendse returning to the back three after being left out as the Springboks levelled the series in Cape Town on Saturday.

Rassie Erasmus promotes Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw to the starting side, having made a late switch of the trio onto the bench ahead of the second Test in an otherwise unchanged forward pack.

Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu continues at fly half with Manie Libbok again offering cover among the replacements in the continuing absence of Handre Pollard.

"It was always our plan to have a little more continuity in player combinations for this series, and we thought that the players who did the job for us last week really showed composure and did well to stick to the plan and what we wanted to achieve last week," said Erasmus.

"Unfortunately, Damian Willemse took a knock in the first half and was not available for selection this weekend, and neither was Handre Pollard, and by sticking to these combinations and making one switch with Cheslin at fullback, we thought it would be the best for this match.

"Kurt-Lee was unlucky not to play last week after Cheslin recovered from his niggle, so we are pleased to see him back. He is a quality player, and his 25 tries in 33 matches so far shows the type of player he is."

The world champions held off an All Blacks fightback to secure a 33-26 victory at Cape Town Stadium, and will now look to ensure that they cannot lose the four-match series as it returns to Johannesburg.

The third Test will be held at FNB Stadium in Soweto before the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series concludes in Baltimore on the east coast of the United States on Saturday 12 September.

It is hoped that Willemse and Pollard will be fit to contend for selection for that encounter. New Zealand are due to name their side on Thursday.

South Africa XV: 1 Ox Nche, 2 Malcolm Marx, 3 Wilco Louw; 4 Eben Etzebeth, 5 Ruan Nortje; 6 Siya Kolisi (capt.), 7 Pieter-Steph du Toit, 8 Jasper Wiese; 9 Cobus Reinach, 10 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu; 11 Ethan Hooker, 12 Damian de Allende, 13 Jesse Kriel, 14 Kurt-Lee Arendse; 15 Cheslin Kolbe.

Replacements: 16 Deon Fourie, 17 Gerhard Steenekamp, 18 Thomas du Toit, 19 Lood de Jager, 20 Andre Esterhuizen, 21 Cameron Hanekom; 22 Morne van den Berg, 23 Manie Libbok.

title: Return to Hamburg: Goalie Swap in the Cup
description: Alex Meyer is returning to his hometown as a BVB goalkeeper: He will take the field in goal for Gregor Kobel in the first round against HEBC. BVB coach Niko Kovac has already announced this. For Meyer...
fullText:
Alex Meyer is returning to his hometown as a BVB goalkeeper: He will take the field in goal for Gregor Kobel in the first round against HEBC. BVB coach Niko Kovac has already announced this. For Meyer, the trip to Hamburg will be a special one: The goalkeeper was born in Bad Oldesloe, 30 km away as the crow flies, and played for the youth teams and the second team of Hamburger SV between 2005 and 2012. Although he was a ball boy at the Volksparkstadion, he never played for the First team there.

Kovac has announced that he'll be rotating the lineup for the cup match: "We'll see how the lads who played over the weekend are feeling." That will determine who starts. Aside from the goalkeeper position, one or two other changes to the starting lineup are already planned.

Ramy Bensebaini has been suspended for two DFB Cup games following his red card in the Super Cup and will miss the match against HEBC, as will the long-term injured Emre Can and Nico Schlotterbeck.

A significant portion of the matchday press conference was devoted to a player who also won't be playing: Giannis Konstantelias tore his cruciate ligament in his first Bundesliga match against HSV—after a strong first half and his first goal for BVB—and will be out indefinitely. Kovac did not want to give an exact prognosis: "We'll have to wait for the surgery first, and then we'll see what exactly was done."

The coach recalls the situation in the second half: "Of course, it was a shock for all of us. It affected my team, but also our fans. You could feel it in the stadium." He describes Konstantelias as "composed, disappointed, very emotional. He'll come back stronger—he's convinced of that, we're convinced of that, and we'll help him." The Greek player will undergo rehabilitation in Dortmund—partly because of the medical care available there, and partly to stay in touch with his teammates: "It's also about being there for him."Christina Reinke

title: Kansas State could be trap game for Arizona State football
description: Arizona State has a difficult schedule, but this looms as the "trap" game in 2026.
fullText:
Arizona State has the most difficult schedule in the Big 12, but is there a game that looks more difficult than one would think?

This looks like a trap game because it is right smack dab in between two huge games for the Sun Devils.

It is the week after ASU faces defending Big 12 champion Texas Tech in Lubbock and right before it hits the road again for a difficult game at BYU.

ASU defeated the Wildcats 24-14 the last time they met, during the 2024 season in Manhattan, Kansas. That game wasn't as close as the score indicates.

Kansas State has a new head coach in Collin Klein, a former player at the school. It also has veteran quarterback Avery Johnson, who has been wildly inconsistent but is in his fourth year as the starter. ASU coach Kenny Dillingham knows him well because he previously recruited Johnson.

This will be the seventh game of the season for both schools.

title: Cleveland Browns practice squad tracker
