title: How Rangers target Kelsy once hid in truck to chase football dream
description: From hiding in a truck to playing in a war zone, Rangers target Kevin Kelsy has had an eventful career already.
fullText:
From hiding in a truck to avoid a travel ban to living through the war in Ukraine, Kevin Kelsy's nascent career has already been a colourful one.

The 22-year-old Portland Timbers striker looks poised to add an interesting new chapter, with a transfer to Rangers reportedly agreed.

But what would the Venezuela forward bring to Ibrox - and what would his move to Glasgow mean for Rangers' existing strikers?

Kelsy began his career in his homeland with Mineros de Guayana, making his debut in 2021 at the age of just 16.

That very early start in top-tier football gives an indication of Kelsy's natural talent, and his actual journey to Mineros shows his determination and his spirit.

To get there, he had to travel 500 miles from his hometown of Valencia. But that hefty distance wasn't the biggest problem - the Covid-19 pandemic meant there was a nationwide travel ban.

So, to avoid detection at checkpoints, he hid in a mining truck.

"It wasn't an appropriate time to be using airports or anything to do with [travel] - so Mineros' president and my agent had an idea," Kelsy said earlier this year, speaking to a Portland Timbers blog.

"Thinking about it, the idea was crazy to be honest. I was so young, I only let myself be guided by my dreams, not thinking about the craziness of what I was doing.

"It was all for my dream, which was to be a professional athlete, to play in Europe."

The year after Kelsy's debut, he began to make his mark, with five goals in 24 appearances.

That led to his dream move to Europe, signing for Shakhtar Donetsk after a very brief spell in Uruguay with Boston River.

Over his two title-winning seasons with Shakhtar, he netted nine goals in 37 appearances to the backdrop of the conflict between Ukraine and Russia.

"It was my first proper experience outside of my country and a very drastic change - both culturally and sporting," he added.

"There were times when I lived first hand the attacks on the country, but also saw how the country defended itself," Kelsy said.

"I won't lie to you, I could see up in the sky war drones getting knocked down.

"They are moments that will forge you, mature you. I think ultimately dreams are bigger than anything else, so I tried not to mind all those things the best I could."

Rangers bolster wing options with signing of Kim

Respite for under-pressure McInnes as Rangers edge out Aberdeen

It was those dreams that again drove him to move - this time to the United States - in search of more regular minutes.

He made his first move to Major League Soccer with a loan spell at FC Cincinnati in 2024.

His six goals in 23 appearances in Ohio was enough to win a move to the Portland Timbers. He has improved his goals-to-games ratio with the Timbers, scoring 16 in 53 matches.

Kelsy's 6ft 4in stature would offer Rangers some of the height in attack they lose as a result of Youssef Chermiti's early season anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Left-footed and physically imposing, the Venezuelan is used to leading an attack.

Timbers general manager Ned Grabavoy outlined the qualities he offers.

"I'm not the tallest guy in the room, but man, I got to say, he's just a solid block," said Grabavoy.

"His work ethic at times - it's almost like he's overworking.

"A big thing with him is to try and show him how to work efficiently, how to work within our group and how to work within our team.

"As he's opened up and got more comfortable during his time here, he's starting to take direction and utilise it and maximise it to be the best version of himself on the field."

Lawrence Shankland was Rangers' marquee summer signing even before Derek McInnes had joined from Hearts.

At Tynecastle, Shankland continued as Hearts captain during McInnes' sole season as head coach and scored 24 goals in 40 games.

McInnes made Shankland the Rangers captain following James Tavernier's departure at the end of last season.

However, the new skipper has not been a regular starter, with three of his six appearances so far this season off the bench. He got his first Premiership goal on Sunday - converting the penalty that defeated Aberdeen.

Chermiti began as a lone striker in the first leg of Rangers' Europa League qualifying defeat by Jagiellonia Bialystok but after his injury, Ryan Naderi took over as McInnes' preferred forward prior to the Aberdeen match, scoring twice in three games.

Miovski, who was in and out of the Rangers team in his debut campaign last term and scored 14 goals in 47 games, has made just one appearance off the bench so far this season. He would appear to be McInnes' least favoured option in attack.

If Kelsy joins, one central striker could leave Ibrox even with Chermiti a long-term absentee - and former Aberdeen striker Miovski would be the favourite to depart.

title: Robinson has Australia tactic to thank for success - Agnew
description: Glenn McGrath-like Ollie Robinson has Australia to thank for bringing back into fashion an age-old tactic which is fuelling his success.
fullText:
After Ollie Robinson's England debut five years ago I said he was the most natural bowler I have seen.

A lot has gone under the bridge since – he was dropped, recalled, dropped again and is now back - but nothing has changed my mind on that.

Using the word robotic to describe him may give the wrong impression. It is a compliment.

Australia's great bowler Glenn McGrath was like that. Everything was utterly rhythmical, repetitive and perfectly grooved.

As a former bowler I watch and see he has inherent rhythm and such a beautiful action. His wrist is just perfect.

Yes, the conditions this summer, in which he has now taken 23 wickets in three matches after England's win in the second Test at Lord's, have been perfect. Robinson would carry them around in his cricket bag if he could.

But the 32-year-old has performed magnificently in them.

Whatever he has wanted the ball to do – to swing in or out or to wobble off the seam – it has done.

He has not needed to go searching for wickets, instead just letting the ball flow naturally from his fingertips.

He will feel like he could take wickets running in blindfolded. There is no better feeling.

Clinical England power to series win over Pakistan

'14,000 runs for a reason' - Root calm on form

Another thing I admire in Robinson is that he is a really good reader of the game.

Tactically, he is extremely sharp. He can spot a batsman's weakness and interpret that into what it means for his own plans very quickly.

A coach told me when he first came into the side that he was a bowler who would give talks to his team-mates about how to get batsmen out even then.

It all adds to what makes him such a good bowler.

Many people will say Robinson's performances this summer show Ben Stokes, Brendon McCullum and managing director Rob Key were wrong to leave him out of their Ashes squad last winter.

Amid talk of a breakdown in trust between Robinson and the Stokes-McCullum regime, they prioritised bowlers with greater pace.

He probably has lost his way with his fitness at different times but I also think back to bowling coach Jon Lewis calling out his fitness in 2022.

There are times Robinson has not been handled as kindly as he might have been.

Perhaps last winter's omission focused his mind, allowing Joe Root to now reap the rewards.

Robinson can also thank Australia for bringing back into the fashion the age-old tactic of the wicketkeeper standing up to the stumps to pace bowlers.

Alex Carey did it so effectively during the Ashes and England are now copying with Robinson.

It may seem obvious but that tweak is really playing into Robinson's strengths.

If the wicketkeeper was stood back the modern batsman would be walking down the pitch to Robinson. With Jamie Smith up they can't because of the risk of being stumped.

It means Robinson can bowl a yard fuller, giving his deliveries more time to swing through the air and means more of Robinson's deliveries would hit the stumps rather than bouncing over from a shorter length.

Of course, you cannot do any of this without a good wicketkeeper. Praise must also go to Jamie Smith.

After we saw Smith struggle badly through the Ashes, he has clearly improved his glovework. Wicketkeeping coach Sarah Taylor has been working him hard before play with a drill where she whacks tennis balls towards him with a racket.

The ball skids through and, with a batsman stood in front edging, missing and hitting the ball, Smith has to stay low and take them.

The results speaks for themselves.

Now the next question for Robinson is whether he can repeat this success on harder, flatter pitches, or in hot conditions which will test those fitness levels. England will face them in their three-Test series in South Africa this winter.

They have often left Robinson out for Test on more batter-friendly pitches but it is time for them to throw him in. He has earned that right.

England are working behind the scenes to get Robinson into the position where he maintains his pace around 82mph, rather than his current place of starting there before dropping to 77 or 78mph.

If he does that, the extra bounce he will get as a result should negate the loss of movement.

And before then I desperately hope England do not rest Robinson, Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson or Josh Tongue for the third Test in Edgbaston.

England's new quartet has shown real promise. They may not have a frontline spinner but Robinson, who conceded runs at just 1.29 per over across the Lord's Test, can effectively do the holding job of a slow bowler if needed.

After their poor run England just need to keep on winning matches and, just as importantly, this group needs to get used to bowling together as an attack.

Joe Root must also learn how to use each of them best.

This, with Robinson as the leader, is England's best attack. Stick with it in Birmingham and beyond.

Jonathan Agnew was speaking to BBC Sport's Matthew Henry

title: Germany's Wamser completes move to Man City
description: Manchester City complete the signing of Bayer Leverkusen and Germany defender Carlotta Wamser on a four-year deal.
fullText:
Manchester City have completed the signing of full-back Carlotta Wamser from Bayer Leverkusen on a four-year deal.

The 22-year-old Germany international, who can play either left-back or right-back, joined Leverkusen from Eintracht Frankfurt on a free transfer in July 2025.

She is City's third signing of the summer after the arrival of defender Niamh Charles from Chelsea and forward Beth Mead from Arsenal.

With Charles among a list of injury absentees, which also includes Grace Clinton, Vivianne Miedema, Jade Rose and Laura Wienroither, Wamser's arrival will be a boost to the WSL champions who start their title defence at home to Birmingham City on Sunday.

Wamser has 14 international caps having come through the German underage system, including being part of the victorious Under-17 European Championship team in 2019.

"I had a perfect welcome here and I already feel very good here and I look forward to my time here in Manchester," she said.

"The English league is the best league in the world and Manchester City is one of the best clubs in the world.

"I feel like I need the next step for my career and I feel that I can develop as a player here. And I like the challenge as well, so I think it's the perfect step for me right now."

City director of football Therese Sjogran added: "We are delighted to welcome Carlotta to the club.

"She is a player we've admired for some time and know she will bring energy, passion and a willingness to learn to the team.

"For such a young, exciting talent to trust us with the next step of her career is something we feel conveys a strong message of what we are building here."

title: England attack's 2005 comparisons fair - Trescothick
description: Comparisons can be made between England’s new-look pace attack and the famous Ashes-winning quartet of 2005, according to interim head coach Marcus Trescothick.
fullText:
Comparisons can be made between England's new-look pace attack and the famous Ashes-winning quartet of 2005, according to interim head coach Marcus Trescothick.

Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue have come together for England in the aftermath of Ben Stokes' retirement and bowled the home side to a series win over Pakistan.

The complementary skills of the new foursome have similarities to the legendary seamers of 21 years ago: Stephen Harmison, Matthew Hoggard, Simon Jones and Andrew 'Freddie' Flintoff.

Trescothick was part of the England team that won back the urn in 2005 and is now in charge for this series before new head coach Stephen Fleming takes over in the winter.

"We do have some real skill, and you look back to 2005 and the sort of comparisons of Harmy, Fred, Simon and Hoggy, you could easily make those sort of comparisons," said Trescothick.

"I'm enjoying the fact we've got four who are match fit at the moment and we've a few [other bowlers] behind it that we're starting to get ready."

Trescothick has presided over a halt to England's previous poor run of only two wins in 10 Tests. Successive victories over Pakistan has given the hosts their first series win since 2024.

The wretched run of form came at what turned out to be the end of Stokes' reign as captain. The all-rounder's retirement not only ushered in Joe Root's second spell as skipper, but also left England looking for a way to balance their XI.

The answer, at least for now, has been to choose four frontline seamers and omit a specialist spinner, with Dan Lawrence offering some part-time off-breaks if required.

And, whereas the England era under Stokes and former head coach Brendon McCullum often put a premium on bowlers with high pace, Robinson's recall after more than two years out of Test cricket looks to have resulted in a more rounded unit.

Robinson's rhythmical action reminiscent of McGrath - Agnew

Pakistan to meet King Charles after Lord's controversy

Archer, Tongue and Atkinson are all capable of high speed, while Robinson often operates below 80mph with the wicketkeeper standing up. His accuracy and ability to extract movement have seen him take 23 wickets this summer at a remarkable average of 8.3.

"We've got a good contrast in what we're trying to do at the moment," said former opener Trescothick.

"What we do have is three guys bowling at 92 miles an hour, which is really nice to have in your armoury and to have the potency in what you're trying to do.

"And the more that they play together and the more experience that everyone gets together, then it fits into place to how you want it to be."

Writing for the Telegraph on Monday, England's captain in 2005 Michael Vaughan said the current attack can only be compared to his bowlers when they win a major series.

But Vaughan added: "They are certainly capable of doing something really special, and winning back the Ashes for England next summer."

England will aim for a 3-0 clean sweep of Pakistan in the third Test at Edgbaston, beginning on 9 September.

The home side will confirm a squad for the series finale in Birmingham in the coming days.

There were seven pace bowlers in the squad for Lord's. Brydon Carse was originally included, only to be removed following an incident outside a nightclub in Derby. He is not expected to be considered for England again until the conclusion of investigations by the police and Cricket Regulator.

In Carse's absence, England's back-up seamers are Sam Cook, Sonny Baker and Matthew Fisher.

The trio have only four Test caps between them, yet Trescothick hinted England are likely to resist the temptation to give the reserves more Test experience.

"First and foremost I want to win the series 3-0, and I think if you're going to do that you want to play the most consistent team possible," said the 50-year-old.

"We've got to see how they all pull up from this game, and they've got four or five days now of break which they've not had for a good period of time because the schedule has been so busy.

"Once we know that then we'll be able to make that decision, but emphasis massively on winning the series 3-0."

title: Man City sign Palmeiras winger Allan for £34m
description: Manchester City complete the signing of winger Allan Elias from Palmeiras in a deal worth up to £34.2m.
fullText:
Manchester City have signed winger Allan Elias from Palmeiras in a deal worth up to £34.2m.

City have paid an initial £32m plus £2.2m in add-ons for the 22-year-old Brazilian, who has signed a five-year contract.

Allan is a direct replacement for compatriot Savio, who completed a £75m move to Tottenham Hotspur last week.

The right-sided winger scored nine goals and provided 12 assists in 96 appearances in all competitions for Brazilian top-flight side Palmeiras after progressing through the club's youth system.

"This is a surreal moment for me. Manchester City, with everything they have won over the past 15 years, are one of the most attractive clubs in the world for players," Allan said.

"To be able to sit here today and say I have joined them is the proudest moment of my life.

"I love Palmeiras and always will - but the decision to come to City was an easy one. I want to be the best footballer I can be and the conversations I've had with the people at City so far has convinced me there isn't a better place for me to fulfil my ambitions."

Allan is the latest addition to Enzo Maresca's squad during a busy summer window.

City have spent over £230m so far this summer with Elliot Anderson arriving from Nottingham Forest for £116m and Ayyoub Bouaddi joining for £85.6m from Lille.

City are in talks with Liverpool over a move for Dutch forward Cody Gakpo and are keen to sign Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

However, City have raised over £286m in player sales with 2026 World Cup Golden Ball winner Rodri making a £65m move to Barcelona, and Tijani Reijnders joining Al-Qadsiah for £52m.

Nico Gonzalez and James Trafford also commanded significant fees, while Omar Marmoush's loan to Tottenham includes an obligation to make the move permanent next summer for £60m.

title: Djokovic in tears during US Open first-round exit
description: An emotional Novak Djokovic suffers a US Open first-round defeat which provides further evidence that age is catching up with the 39-year-old great.
fullText:
Novak Djokovic broke down in tears during a US Open first-round defeat by Argentina's Mariano Navone which provided further evidence age is fast catching up with the 39-year-old great.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion was overcome by emotion in the deciding set of a dramatic match where he struggled physically throughout and had to vomit into a towel bin.

Djokovic, seeded fourth, showed the fight for which he has always been renowned before succumbing to a 7-6 (7-5) 5-7 4-6 6-2 6-1 loss in a humid New York.

It was the first time the Serb had been beaten in the opening round at Flushing Meadows and the first time he had lost in the opening round of a Grand Slam tournament since 2006.

"I think it was obvious that it was an awful feeling on the court for me," Djokovic said.

"I don't want to take too much out of Mariano's win. Congrats to him, he's a nice guy and a fighter - but I didn't enjoy myself."

Djokovic managed to raise a smile as he congratulated 25-year-old Navone on what will rank as one of the biggest victories of the world number 49's career.

But, after showing grace and class while congratulating his opponent, a disconsolate Djokovic was unable to keep a brave face for long and appeared close to tears again as he trudged back to the locker room.

The defeat ended Djokovic's latest bid for a standalone record 25th Grand Slam singles title, which would move him clear of Australia's Margaret Court.

Chances are clearly running out for Djokovic. Many sensed this was another decent opportunity given world number one Jannik Sinner is missing through injury and defending champion Carlos Alcaraz is making his comeback from a long-term wrist injury.

Venus Williams loses 15th match in row in 2am finish

Why tough US Open draw will be true test of Alcaraz's fitness

Djokovic had reached at least the semi-finals at six of the previous seven Grand Slams going into the US Open, but the manner in which he struggled in the humid conditions was a worrying sight for his supporters.

Djokovic looked nauseous throughout a tense encounter and he appeared to be dealing with a similar issue to the one which affected him at the Cincinnati Open two weeks ago.

In his only appearance on the North American hard courts before heading to New York, Djokovic wilted in similarly humid conditions in a shock early exit to Argentina's Thiago Tirante.

Afterwards Djokovic revealed he had been hampered by a "health condition" which has been "bothering" him in oppressive conditions over a number of years and, discussing the issue with reporters shortly after losing to Navone, called it a "serious issue".

"It's something that I have been carrying pretty much every match this year - vomiting, throwing up," Djokovic said.

"And then my whole body starts to collapse basically, cramping and pain - the back just gave up in the end and shoulder, and I couldn't close it out."

Djokovic made a promising start as he broke Navone's serve at the first attempt, only to see a 4-1 advantage wiped out as he began to struggle in the humid conditions.

The catalyst for Djokovic's troubles appeared to be a lengthy rally which sapped him of energy and left him struggling to recover.

A flustered Djokovic seemed to drop speed in both his serve and groundstrokes, calling out the doctor after the ninth game for some tablets to help alleviate what was bothering him.

He continued to look distressed as the opener moved into the tie-break - wearily bowing his head and bending over double between points - as Navone maintained his focus to strike first after one hour and 13 minutes.

As Djokovic toiled, an eerie hush fell around Arthur Ashe Stadium which indicated the crowd's growing concern for the four-time champion.

The physical problems did continue to linger, but Djokovic perked up enough - seemingly helped by the cooler conditions under the roof - to level the match.

Djokovic becoming more animated in the early part of third set was a surefire sign he was starting to feel more like his old self, as was how he pounced on a poor service game from Navone to break for 5-4 and move ahead.

These are the positions from which prime Djokovic would usually go on to win, even when he was struggling physically.

The fact he was unable to do that against Navone, who has never gone past the second round in New York, was another indication of his declining powers.

What had been a tight match quickly ran away from Djokovic and became a difficult watch for the thousands still inside Ashe as local time fast approached midnight.

The atmosphere became subdued again as it became clear that Djokovic was not going to be able to wriggle out of trouble on this occasion.

Despite the clear signs of sickness, it was hard to ignore the feeling that Djokovic's distress could also have been down to the realisation his ageing body is starting to struggle to meet the physical demands needed at the highest level.

Questions have been put to Djokovic over several years about when he might decide to hang up his racquet. Answers have always been honest - but with a sense of exasperation and indignation.

In a new documentary released earlier this month, Djokovic insists he has not put an "expiry date" on his career.

"Why would I talk about retirement when I still keep proving to myself that I can still win?" he declares.

Losing to Navone at a Grand Slam event on which he places so much importance, particularly so soon after being beaten by Tirante, must surely set off some alarm bells for Djokovic.

But, speaking shortly after coming off court, he said finding a solution to the unspecified health problem remains his immediate plan.

Retirement, it seems, has still not entered his mind - even when his emotions were as raw as we have seen in a long time.

title: Driven & hungry Rashford a Man Utd asset - Maguire
description: Manchester United defender Harry Maguire is backing Marcus Rashford to make a big impact at the club this season.
fullText:
Manchester United defender Harry Maguire is confident Marcus Rashford will have a significant impact at the club this season.

The 28-year-old started his first Premier League game for United in 21 months in the 5-2 victory over Ipswich at Old Trafford, and was one of his side's main attacking threats.

Having a future at United seemed unlikely when he fell out with former boss Ruben Amorim and was loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, where he would have stayed had the Catalans activated a £26m transfer fee.

With the transfer window closing on Tuesday night, it now looks certain Rashford will remain at his boyhood club.

"He's a great talent," said Maguire. "He's always a threat.

"If Marcus wants to be here, wants to work, wants to improve and help the team, of course we're willing to have him in the team.

"He could still do a lot more and I think he'll say he can do more but if we keep him fit, we keep him happy, he keeps driven and hungry, he's a great asset to have."

There has been plenty of negativity around Rashford, even dating back to Erik ten Hag's time at the club.

His work-rate and commitment have been questioned as well as the basic question of whether he actually enjoys the game any more.

Rashford did appear to benefit from working with Unai Emery and Hansi Flick during his time away from Old Trafford and the fact head coach Michael Carrick knows him well is felt to be an advantage.

"You've got to remember Marcus has had a wonderful career for this club," said Maguire.

"But when you play at this club for numerous years, there's going to be bad seasons, and when the bad seasons come everyone piles on you. That's part and parcel of playing for this club.

"As a club, we haven't been perfect from top to bottom. We haven't been challenging at the top end. So, Marcus has been part of a rough ride for Manchester United.

"When that happens, players get dug out. I've been through it," added Maguire, who also looked to be leaving the club at one stage after losing both his place in the team and the captaincy under former boss Erik ten Hag.

"He's come back in, really fit and sharp and we're excited to have him."

Carrick describes Rashford as being like a new signing and while the United boss rejuvenated midfielder Kobbie Mainoo after he was repeatedly overlooked by predecessor Amorim, he now has to lift his spirits again after England boss Thomas Tuchel did not play him at the World Cup.

Mainoo also started for the first time this season against Ipswich and grew into the game after United went behind.

"I thought he was brilliant," said Maguire.

"To say he hasn't had many minutes in pre-season, he was magnificent.

"His work without the ball has improved so much since Michael's been in. He's becoming a real monster in there, wins a lot of second balls and a lot of duels.

"The thing is he's so young. If we want him to play for this club for another 10 years, there's going to be times where he's going to go through a patch like I spoke about with Rashy and myself.

"But that's part and parcel. He's really level-headed, really composed and has great belief in his ability.

"He's going to be a magnificent player for this club for many years."

With Rashford staying at United, Netherlands forward Joshua Zirkzee appears to be the most likely senior player to leave the club before the transfer window closes.

However, a proposed loan move to Serie A outfit Fiorentina for the 25-year-old has now been scrapped.

It is possible Juventus might come in for the Netherlands forward, who has been an unused substitute for both Manchester United games so far, although that is dependent on Canada forward Jonathan David completing a move to Atletico Madrid.

That might be key in whether United make additions to Carrick's squad, and he did not totally rule the possibility of new arrivals after yesterday's 5-2 victory over Ipswich at Old Trafford.

"It's always difficult to say, to be honest, when there's so little time left but we're always open if there's something else to be able to add," he said.

"I wouldn't shut that down, but as it stands, we'll have to wait and see."

title: The transfers to watch before window closes
description: BBC Sport's football experts picks out the standout transfers that could go through before Tuesday's 23:00 BST English deadline.
fullText:
The summer transfer window may have been open since 15 June but several Premier League clubs are still scrambling to get key deals over the line before Tuesday's 23:00 BST deadline.

From Julian Alvarez and Enzo Fernandez to Cody Gakpo and Ismaila Sarr, some of football's biggest names could yet be on the move.

But they will have to battle the clock to earn their dream moves before the market closes.

With that in mind, BBC Sport's football reporters have picked out the high-profile moves which could go through during what promises to be a busy ending to the window.

Julian Alvarez's potential move to Arsenal could be the biggest deal to watch, with the Atletico Madrid striker's future now hanging in the balance.

The 26-year-old is caught between his desire to leave Atletico and the club's refusal to sell him to Barcelona. But they would do a deal with Arsenal.

The Gunners have had a long-term interest in Alvarez and have been monitoring the dramatic situation, with Atleti looking for a fee of 150m euros (£128m).

Alvarez has missed multiple training sessions and did not travel to face Sevilla on Saturday, with Simeone saying he wasn't well enough.

Simeone, meanwhile, has attempted to keep the door open, saying he will "do everything" he can to make Alvarez feel important when he returns to training.

Enzo Fernandez missed Sunday's Premier League win over Brighton and his future is under increasing uncertainty, having been linked with a big-money move to Manchester City.

Enzo Maresca worked with the Argentina midfielder at Chelsea and needs to bolster his ranks following the departures of Rodri, Bernardo Silva, Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders this summer.

Any potential move would likely be a club record deal, surpassing the £116m paid for Elliot Anderson earlier this summer.

Fernandez potentially leaving for Manchester City could open the door for fellow midfielder Lamine Camara to arrive at Stamford Bridge from Monaco as his replacement.

It could be Chelsea's 13th deal coming in, with exits exceeding 30 players as the Blues are expected to surpass the Premier League player sales record they set at £300m last season.

There is further intrigue around departures with Mykhailo Mudryk looking for a loan move and still a lack of clarity on the futures of Pedro Neto and Tosin Adarabioyo. The likes of Dario Essugo, Deivid Washington and Shim Mheuka could also leave.

Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool about signing attacker Cody Gakpo and the Netherlands international is open to the move.

But Liverpool would only be willing to sanction the transfer if they can bring in one more attacking player, in addition to Bradley Barcola.

Spurs are also interested but City are willing to offer a deal worth around £85m and sources indicate that City is Gakpo's preferred destination.

With Gakpo's future up in the air, Liverpool have turned their attentions to Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr after having two bids for Yankuba Minteh rejected by Brighton.

The Seagulls want more than the £60m offered by Liverpool and it remains to be seen whether Iraola's side go back in for him.

Like the Gambian, Sarr is a right-sided winger and the Reds initially enquired about the Senegal international last week, but that was rebuffed by Crystal Palace.

Tottenham are in advanced talks to sign Iliman Ndiaye from Everton, with Richarlison set to move in the opposite direction.

Although a deal for Ndiaye is largely agreed between the two clubs, it remains unclear whether he will make the switch to north London, with Manchester City among the clubs to have expressed an interest.

Everton are open to selling Ndiaye, 26, after he rejected multiple contract offers and held talks with Saudi club Al-Hilal earlier this summer.

Meanwhile, Everton have agreed terms in principle to re-sign striker Richarlison after he told Spurs head coach Roberto de Zerbi "too many times that he wants to leave".

Everton are growing increasingly confident of completing a loan deal to bring Jack Grealish back from Manchester City, although the precise terms of any agreement remain complicated as the England international enters the final year of his contract at Etihad Stadium.

Grealish has prioritised a return to Everton, where he spent last season on loan, over the option of rejoining his boyhood club Aston Villa, who have also expressed an interest.

Just a few hours after the unveiling of Nico Gonzalez, Matthias Jaissle made it clear he would continue to push for further deals in the final throes of the window.

Another forward is on the German's wishlist and Newcastle have a longstanding interest in Lille's Matias Fernandez-Pardo, whose creativity and ability to play in a number of positions across the frontline is a huge draw. The 21-year-old also fits the age range Newcastle have targeted this summer.

This would be a complicated deal to do in the final days of the window, but it was a little telling that Lille manager Davide Ancelotti left Fernandez-Pardo out of his squad for the weekend's game against Paris St-Germain and has decided to exclude him from training until the window shuts.

Unless there is a very late, and unexpected, development around Marcus Rashford, it feels as if Manchester United's deadline-day business will centre around Joshua Zirkzee and the smaller deals they can do.

Fiorentina wanted to take the Netherlands forward on loan, with an option to buy.

United, ideally, would prefer to sell, or at least get a loan with an obligation.

With no agreement possible, Fiorentina are now looking elsewhere.

However, Juventus are keen on Zirkzee, although a move for the 25-year-old hinges on Canada forward Jonathan David leaving for Atletico Madrid.

Zirkzee's exit might open the door for a left-back or a reinforcement in the forward department, although that too might initially be a loan.

title: Seattle Mariners to Promote Top 100 Prospect to Major Leagues
description: Lazaro Montes, the Mariners power-hitting outfield prospect, will be getting his big league break.
fullText:
The Seattle Mariners are coming off a disappointing sweep at the hands of the Toronto Blue Jays this weekend at the Rogers Centre in Toronto.

The series sweep was accentuated with a 7-0, shutout loss against the Blue Jays on Sunday, which capped off the first leg of a six-game road trip for the Mariners.

The next leg of Seattle's road trip will be against the Boston Red Sox, with game one set to begin at 3:45 p.m. PT on Monday at Fenway Park in Boston.

During the series, the Mariners will be joined by one of the potent power hitters in the minor leagues.

According to a report on "X" from baseball reporter Francys Romero, which was later corroborated by Seattle Times reporter Ryan Divish, Seattle will be calling up top 100 prospect/outfielder Lazaro Montes when active major league rosters expand from 26 to 28 players Sept. 1.

Montes is ranked as the 56th prospect in baseball per MLB Pipeline and has developed a reputation as one of, if not the best home run hitter, in the minor leagues.

Montes began the season with the Double-A Arkansas Travelers before he was promoted to the Triple-A Tacoma Rainiers on July 7.

Since being promoted to Triple-A, Montes has slashed .274/.369/.571 with a .940 OPS in 44 games and has hit 13 doubles and 13 home runs with 30 RBIs.

Across the entire season, the 6-foot-5, 250-pound outfielder .249/.369/.558 with a .927 OPS in 123 games and has hit 24 doubles, a triple and 38 homers and 96 RBIs.

Lazaro Montes with his 24th double. pic.twitter.com/YjEYh5w64p

Montes first joined the Mariners organization as an international free agent out of Cuba on Jan. 15, 2022. He was a part of a stacked international recruiting class that also included fellow top 100 prospect, infielder/outfielder Michael Arroyo.

The 21-year-old mainly plays right field, and hits left-handed, both roles currently handled by on-and-off designated hitters Dominic Canzone and Taylor Ward.

Ward, who's provided some right-handed hitting coverage on the team's roster, has struggled since the team acquired him in a trade with the Baltimore Orioles on Aug. 3.

Canzone has received more regular at-bats against left-handed pitchers. According to an article from Seattle Times reporter Adam Jude, Montes is expected to receive regular at-bats with Seattle, which will likely lead to lineups with both Canzone and Montes in them.

Following their loss against Toronto, the Mariners are five games out of first place in the American League West and five games out of the final wild card spot in the American League.

title: Titans release $3M dual-threat quarterback in a surprising move after cutting Will Levis
description: The Tennessee Titans made some surprising decisions with their QB room on Sunday. After cutting Will Levis it seemed like the QB room was set, but that was not the case.
fullText:
Titans release $3M dual-threat quarterback in a surprising move after cutting Will Levis originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Tennessee Titans are looking to take somewhat of a step forward under Robert Saleh in his first year as head coach. However, it will not be easy, as they still have a young roster that they hope will mature as the season progresses.

On Sunday, Tennessee had to make several decisions, just like the rest of the league. The Titans finally cut ties with Will Levis in a move that felt overdue.

"Will Levis was at one time the hopeful future of the Tennessee Titans at quarterback, but that time has passed and he's leaving Nashville. The No. 33 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Levis is being waived by Tennessee, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported Sunday. The team later announced the news," NFL.com's Grant Gordon wrote.

The move to release Levis seemed to open the door for former Tennessee Volunteer Hendon Hooker.

"Tennessee Football legend Hendon Hooker looked to have made the Tennessee Titans' 53-man roster, but that wouldn't be the case. The former Volunteer quarterback was going to survive a crowded quarterback room to earn his spot on the roster after it seemed he notably beat out former Kentucky Wildcat and 2nd-round pick Will Levis to make the roster," SI's Major Passons wrote.

However, that was far from the reality. Tennessee also decided to move on from Hooker, releasing two quarterbacks on the same day. It was a surprising move, and one that SI's Caleb Sisk called a joke.

"The Titans ended up cutting Hendon Hooker anyways… what a joke," Sisk posted.

The Titans will likely try to sign Hooker to the practice squad if he clears waivers, but it is risky to have only one backup quarterback on the roster. Tennessee is in an interesting position heading into the regular season.

Hooker has made $3 million in his career so far. He also had a solid preseason, which is another factor in why this decision was perceived as shocking. Despite his performance, the Titans ultimately decided to move in a different direction at quarterback.

title: Steelers Make Decision on QB Room for 2026 Season
description: The Pittsburgh Steelers have made a decision on who to keep at quarterback ahead of the 2026 season.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have decided to carry all four quarterbacks heading into the 2026 season: Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Drew Allar, and Will Howard.

Rodgers will be the starter as he enters his final season in the league. The 42-year-old completed 65.7 percent of his passes for 3,322 yards, 24 touchdowns, and seven interceptions in the 2025 season for the Steelers.

The four-time MVP is no longer in his prime, but he is still an accurate passer and led Pittsburgh to an AFC North title and a playoff appearance last season.

Behind Rodgers, the Steelers have veteran Mason Rudolph as the backup. Rudolph has completed 64.4 percent of his passes for 4,925 yards, 30 touchdowns, and 22 interceptions in his six years in the league. He should be a stable backup behind Rodgers.

Pittsburgh's future quarterback could be either Will Howard or Drew Allar. Howard is entering his second year in the league and had a prolific 2024 season at Ohio State. In that campaign, he completed 73 percent of his passes for 4,010 yards, 35 touchdowns, and 10 interceptions while rushing for 226 yards and seven touchdowns.

In the preseason, Howard completed 26 of 40 passes for 229 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions.

Allar had a solid collegiate career at Penn State as a three-year starter, completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 7,402 yards, 61 touchdowns, and 13 interceptions while adding 732 yards and 12 touchdowns on the ground.

Allar was solid in the preseason, completing 30 of 54 passes for 351 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception.

Howard and Allar both showed flashes in the preseason, and one of them could develop into the future starter for the Steelers.

Pittsburgh has a talented roster heading into the 2026 season as they look to win a second-straight division title and make it back to the playoffs. However, they have a new head coach, with Mike McCarthy taking over for Mike Tomlin.

With Rodgers' familiarity with McCarthy, the Steelers should be competitive despite the talent of other AFC North teams, including the Baltimore Ravens and Cincinnati Bengals.

title: Bills Release 9-Year Veteran WR as 53-Man Roster Set
description: The Buffalo Bills have named their 53-man roster and the team released a veteran wide receiver who had a good camp. The post Bills Release 9-Year Veteran WR as 53-Man Roster Set appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills have named their 53-man roster.

Buffalo announced their roster cuts on Sunday evening, and one of the notable cuts was veteran wide receiver Trent Sherfield. The Bills brought back Sherfield on a one-year deal, and he was competing for a roster spot, but obviously didn't do enough.

Bills insider Alex Brasky of SI revealed that Sherfield is a practice squad candidate for Buffalo to add more depth at receiver.

"Also interesting that Trent Sherfield has been cut. Might be an option for the practice squad," Brasky wrote on X.

Sherfield played for the Bills in 2023. In his lone year with Buffalo, Sherfield recorded 11 receptions for 86 yards and a touchdown. He's entering his ninth NFL season and spent last season between the Denver Broncos and Arizona Cardinals, and also ended the year on the New England Patriots' practice squad during the playoffs.

In his NFL career, Sherfield has appeared in 124 games, recording 89 receptions for 1,034 yards and 6 touchdowns.

After Sherfield bounced around three different teams last year, he knew he needed to find stability.

He ended up signing a one-year deal with the Bills, which he was excited about as he called it a full-circle moment.

"It's been tough, not going to lie," Sherfield told GNN Sports after practice Monday. "Last year was really tough. First time being cut in eight years. … It was a lot of moving around. It was really tough on me mentally, obviously tough on my family too. But I think it's a full-circle moment coming back here."

Sherfield, meanwhile, said after getting cut by the Broncos, his perspective on his future changed.

"A lot of people get cut. Top guys get released all the time and I think it's just a perspective change," Sherfield said. "… My perspective has changed a lot. … I just told myself that I wasn't going to allow my career to end like that. I've always told myself that I want to go out on my own terms and that the league would never push me out."

Sherfield signed as an undrafted free agent in 2018 with the Cardinals.

title: Sean McVay on Aaron Donald: We'll see if we think it’s best to play him in Australia
description: Now that Aaron Donald is officially back with the Rams, when will he play?
fullText:
Now that Aaron Donald is officially back with the Rams, when will he play?

Head coach Sean McVay didn't rule out Donald potentially playing in Australia when the Rams open the season against the 49ers. But he also didn't want to put a timetable on anything for the three-time AP defensive player of the year.

"I'm not going to talk about any sort of plans, it's going to be a day at a time for us," McVay said in his Sunday press conference. "What does that mean for Australia? The first step was, alright, if you're coming back, let's do that, let's get you back on the practice field, let's get you acclimated to your teammates, to your coaches. And then we'll see what that ramp-up period looks like, whether or not he's available or whether or not we think it's best to play him in Australia. I think the best way to do it is take it one day at a time.

"But, we're obviously excited to be able to have him back."

As he has throughout the summer, McVay noted how much Donald means to him personally when discussing his enthusiasm for the defensive tackle's return.

"It's way bigger than football," McVay said. "There's a lot of history. There's a lot of experiences that we've shared. A lot of love for each other's families. So, I know for him to want to be able to explore this and come back into the mix is a real credit to the special people that he's got a chance to be around, and that's his teammates, and that's obviously his coaches. And excited to start this journey.

So how did it get to this point?

"I think he wanted to get to a point where he knows just from his previous experiences, alright, I want to be able to be there, be a part of the football team, and I think there were some things that he wanted to be able to work through — just in terms of his workouts and where he felt his body was before he could comfortably get to this spot," McVay said. "And so, that was really what went into it.

"He and I both kind of had an unspoken understanding like, once we get the roster down, where are you at with it? You don't owe us anything. And no matter what, there's a lot of love. We wanted to make sure that he felt good about doing that. He obviously is incredibly — his priority is with his family. And so when he does something, he does it all in. That's what led to being able to get it done today."

title: Seahawks Keep Hard Knocks Fan Favorite on 53-Man Roster
description: A Seahawks Hard Knocks favorite reportedly survived final cuts after going from substitute teaching and real estate back to an NFL roster. The post Seahawks Keep Hard Knocks Fan Favorite on 53-Man Roster appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks are officially keeping one of the breakout personalities from their season of HBO's Hard Knocks.

Wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr. has made Seattle's initial 53-man roster,the team announced on Sunday, August 30, as the team worked through its final cuts.

For Foster, making the team would complete one of the more unlikely journeys on Seattle's roster. He went from an undrafted rookie whose first NFL opportunity ended because of injury, to substitute teaching and selling real estate, to becoming one of the players viewers have gotten to know during Hard Knocks.

And unlike many feel-good training camp stories, this one appears to have ended with a roster spot.

Foster's path back to Seattle became a featured storyline during Episode 3 of Hard Knocks.

The Seahawks' official recap noted that Foster spent time with Seattle as an undrafted free agent in 2025 before an injury derailed his first opportunity. After leaving the team, Foster returned home, worked as a substitute teacher and earned his real estate license before eventually getting another opportunity with the Seahawks.

That story continued to get television time as Foster fought for a roster spot.

Gregg Bell of The News Tribune reported that Foster had even substituted at his former high school, St. Edward in Ohio, including an assignment covering a Latin class despite acknowledging he did not know Latin.

His NFL comeback was about more than a television storyline, however.

Foster caught five passes for 36 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's first preseason game, then added receptions of 24 and 13 yards over the Seahawks' final two exhibitions. He finished the preseason with seven catches for 73 yards and a touchdown.

That production gave the Seahawks a football reason to keep him after Hard Knocks gave fans a reason to root for him.

title: Packers Place Former 3rd-Round Pick on Injured Reserve
description: One of the big questions facing the Green Bay Packers was who and how many wide receivers would make the roster. As it turns out, the team will place a second-year wide receiver on the Injured Reserve with a designation to return. This will free up a roster spot for the team, allowing them to […] The post Packers Place Former 3rd-Round Pick on Injured Reserve appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
One of the big questions facing the Green Bay Packers was who and how many wide receivers would make the roster. As it turns out, the team will place a second-year wide receiver on the Injured Reserve with a designation to return. This will free up a roster spot for the team, allowing them to keep an extra wide receiver.

Savion Williams suffered an ankle injury in the Packers' second preseason game against the Denver Broncos. He will now miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season, as the team will ease him back in.

The Packers' wide receiver room was deep. They had their three starters set. Matthew Golden, Jayden Reed, and Christian Watson were going to start for the team. Then, they had Williams, Skyy Moore, Bo Melton, J.Michael Sturdivant, Isaiah Neyor, and Will Sheppard.

Green Bay wound up releasing Neyor and Sheppard. They placed Williams on the IR, allowing them to keep Moore, Melton, and Sturdivant as the last three receivers on the depth chart.

All three provide special teams value. Moore is going to be their return option. Melton is the team's top special teams gunner, and Sturdivant made the team with a strong ability to make plays on special teams.

Packers General Manager Brian Gutekunst discussed the possibility of keeping seven receivers on the roster. He noted that the team had done it before, but it is an uncommon strategy. Williams not being healthy enough put him in a position where the team did not need to make that decision.

For Williams, it puts the brakes on what was expected to be a year where we learn what he really can bring to the table. He was a third-round pick, but fell to 87th overall because of questions about his usage and role. His first year did not quite ease concerns.

The versatile playmaker had just 11 rushes for 37 yards and 10 targets for 78 yards. His average target depth was 1.7 yards down the field, so he was not bringing much to the passing game. Green Bay was expected to put more on his plate in year two.

With the top three receivers defined in their roles, the team was expected to use Williams as the ultimate gadget weapon. Now, the gadget player missed the last week of the preseason and is going to miss the next four weeks. It will be even harder to integrate him into the offense when he gets back, given his specific role on the offense.

It is not going to completely derail the second-year of Williams, but it is going to put things on pause for what felt like a make-or-break season.

title: Undrafted Patriots Rookie Earns Roster Spot With Unusual Position Switch
description: Undrafted rookie Tanner Arkin learned a second position during the preseason, and that unusual move helped him claim a spot on the Patriots’ initial roster.
fullText:
Undrafted Patriots Rookie Earns Roster Spot With Unusual Position Switch originally appeared on NESN. 

Tanner Arkin found a creative path onto the New England Patriots' initial 53-man roster.

The undrafted rookie arrived as a tight end, impressed as an in-line blocker and then expanded his responsibilities by taking preseason snaps at fullback. That versatility helped Arkin survive Sunday's roster deadline.

The Patriots kept Arkin alongside Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon and fullback Reggie Gilliam, according to the team's position-by-position roster breakdown. New England released tight ends C.J. Dippre and Jack Westover.

Arkin began generating attention early in training camp because of his blocking. He eventually received first-team opportunities in early-down and short-yardage packages, an encouraging sign for any undrafted rookie trying to make an NFL roster.

The Patriots then gave him work at fullback during the preseason.

His performance there was not flawless, but it revealed how New England could use him. Arkin can provide depth behind Gilliam, contribute on field goals and kickoff returns and potentially enter the game in run-heavy packages near the goal line or in short-yardage situations. He also gives offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels another option for preserving two-back formations if Gilliam is unavailable.

Arkin is unlikely to become a major receiving option with Henry and Raridon ahead of him at tight end. His route to playing time will depend on blocking, special teams and his ability to line up in multiple spots. That may sound like a limited role, but it can be extremely valuable for a team trying to maximize every game-day roster position.

The Patriots announce they've released the following players:

S Mike Brown
S Eric Butler
G Mehki Butler
OL Jack Conley
CB Brandon Crossley
OL Darrian Dalcourt
WR Nick DeGennaro
CB Marcellas Dial Jr.
TE C.J. Dippre

WR Cameron Dorner
LB Amari Gainer
DT Eric Gregory
P…

Keeping a fourth conventional tight end would have been difficult to justify. Keeping a player who can function as a tight end, emergency fullback and special teams blocker is a different proposition.

Arkin's roster spot also offers another clue about how the Patriots could structure their offense. New England has invested in its running game with Rhamondre Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and newly acquired Corey Kiner, while the offensive line enters the season with far more stability than it has had in recent years.

MORE: Patriots Cut Unlikely Training Camp Interception Leader After Roster Shakeup

Having Gilliam and Arkin available gives McDaniels the personnel to use heavier formations and force defenses to account for multiple rushing possibilities.

Undrafted players rarely make a roster by remaining one-dimensional. Arkin recognized his opportunity, embraced an unfamiliar assignment and turned it into a job.

Now the Patriots have an intriguing hybrid player whose value may extend well beyond the traditional tight end depth chart.

title: J.J. McCarthy Issued Compelling Dolphins Trade Idea Amid Vikings’ Decision
description: On Aug. 30, the Minnesota Vikings announced their 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season. Moreover, the team’s intriguing decision was to go with four QBs, including J.J. McCarthy.
fullText:
On Aug. 30, the Minnesota Vikings announced their 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season. Moreover, the team's intriguing decision was to go with four QBs, including J.J. McCarthy.McCarthy looks to be QB3 behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. With Murray and Wentz having an injury history, McCarthy might be an insurance policy in case injuries hit both. However, the Vikings might know that the former first-round pick has some trade value.Any team needing QB help during the season leading up to the trade deadline might call the Vikings over McCarthy. For Mark Powell of FanSided, the Miami Dolphins make sense for the Vikings QB.In an Aug. 30 article, Powell proposed a trade that would see the Dolphins acquire McCarthy in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick. Miami already landed quarterback Kyle McCord in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick. As a result, Miami probably didn't want to spend much on a backup QB, but if they run into any issues under center, perhaps McCarthy might be an option. "Dumping a former first-round pick is never easy," Powell wrote. "Still, the Dolphins fourth rounder is essentially a late Day 2 pick (since it could very well be the first pick in that round). "The Vikings are a quarterback away from making the postseason, which is why their decision to draft McCarthy, and punt on Kirk Cousins and eventually Sam Darnold, all the more confusing. That is neither here nor there."

As for the Dolphins, they appear content with their two-QB setup for now and will address any issues midseason. Still, Powell argues that someone like McCarthy would be a more reliable option than McCord, who lacks experience in regular-season games. McCord signed with the Packers in January after spending the 2025 season on the Philadelphia Eagles' practice squad after they selected him in the sixth round of last year's draft."Willis is a dual-threat quarterback, which is exciting but also makes him prone to hard contact," Powell added in his article. "Even if Miami intends to tank this season, they'll need someone reliable behind Willis just in case. "I might recommend a veteran backup — which McCarthy is not — but I also wouldn't be tanking as heavily as Jon-Eric Sullivan."

For now, it appears the Dolphins are going with two QBs, but that doesn't mean another team can't call Minnesota for McCarthy. For now, he'll just have to work behind the scenes until an opportunity comes, whether it's in Minnesota or elsewhere.The former Michigan Wolverines product didn't play the preseason finale due to injury, and former NFL player Chad Johnson believes that being injury-prone could be what dooms McCarthy. "I don't know how serious his ankle injury was, but one of the issues that he does have is that he's been injured most of the time since he's been there," Johnson said on the Aug. 28 edition of "Nightcap." "Here we go, we're in the preseason, and you're injured again. "Maybe he thinks his spot is safe. He's one of the few who needs to come in and be playing in a game like this to show that he still has it, because he might be auditioning as well for another team."

title: Green Bay Packers: how being on the commissioner exempt list could affect length of possible Josh Jacobs suspension
description: The Green Bay Packers had a plan for running back throughout the course of the 2026 NFL offseason. Unfortunately, Josh Jacobs getting arrested in May on five charges, including a felony. Obviously, this threw a possible wrench in Green Bay’s plans. Over the course of the last several weeks, there have been rumblings that Jacobs […] The post Green Bay Packers: how being on the commissioner exempt list could affect length of possible Josh Jacobs suspension appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers had a plan for running back throughout the course of the 2026 NFL offseason. Unfortunately, Josh Jacobs getting arrested in May on five charges, including a felony. Obviously, this threw a possible wrench in Green Bay's plans.

Over the course of the last several weeks, there have been rumblings that Jacobs could be suspended by the NFL. This notion gained traction last week when he was formerly charged on two counts. Jacobs was handed down a charge for battery and another for destruction of property. Both of these are misdemeanors.

On Sunday, the day that every NFL team had to trim their rosters from 90 to 53, Roger Goddell decided to place Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list. While on this list, the Packers running back will continue to collect a paycheck. However, he will not be allowed to practice with the team, play in games, or even step foot in Green Bay football facilities.

Rob Demovsky of ESPN shared the following interpretation of what the collective bargaining agreement says regarding players on the commissioner exempt list:

If my understanding of this is correct, time spent on the commissioner exempt list counts toward a future suspension.

Say if in Week 4, the NFL announces a 6-game suspension for Josh Jacobs, he would only miss 3 more games (but loses 6 games of $).

Correct me if I’m wrong. https://t.co/YX0Akpl8lU

— Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) August 30, 2026

As one can see, the number of games Jacobs spends on the exempt list will count towards the number of games he is potentially suspended. If he is indeed suspended, he will have to forfeit salary to make up for the number of games it is for.

In other words, say he is on the exempt list for the first three games and then is handed a six-game suspension. He would only miss three more games and would not be paid for those games. However, he also will have to forfeit his salary for the first three games.

With Jacobs out, Marshawn Lloyd will be the starting running back in Green Bay. Kaleb Johnson was acquired via trade amid the news from the NFL and will likely serve as the backup. Chris Brooks, who signed a two-year contract earlier this year, will be the third running back on the roster.

The San Francisco 49ers have had quite the offseason, and to put it frankly, they probably (above a lot of other NFL teams) are the most eager to get back on the gridiron to get this 2026 campaign underway.

One development throughout training camp was the Niners sustaining a plethora of injuries to their pass catchers, and the uncertainty of George Kittle's status before Week 1.

Early in training camp, newly signed Christian Kirk sustained a calf injury, which has landed him on Injured Reserve to start the campaign. San Francisco also announced that Isaac Guerendo has landed on the PUP list to begin the season.

More NFL on Heavy: San Francisco 49ers Announce Isaac Guerendo Decision Before Roster Deadline

As the roster deadline has passed, wide receiver Christian Kirk will begin the 2026 season on the Injured Reserve list with his calf injury, which is now officially more serious than most analysts initially thought.

Christian Kirk (calf) to begin season on IR; will miss at least 4 games.

— Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) August 30, 2026

Kirk will have to miss the first four games of the season, but it's not believed to be a season-ending injury, so Kirk updates will likely be in the future once the season begins.

As for Kirk, it's no surprise that the team will be patient with him. It's one of the benefits of the Injured Reserve. He has experience in ways that Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins do not in the NFL as receivers. Plus, Kirk has production. He will add an element to the passing game the Niners have been missing once he returns.

Christian Kirk is an NFL veteran of eight seasons.

Kirk played in 13 games for the Houston Texans in 2025 and hauled in 28 passes for 239 yards and one touchdown.

Originally drafted by the Arizona Cardinals, Kirk also spent three seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

title: Packers trade for RB Kaleb Johnson at cutdown deadline
description: Kaleb Johnson was the 83rd overall pick in the 2025 draft
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers have added depth to their running back room on Sunday, as they've traded for former Pittsburgh Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson. Johnson, a 23-year-old, was a third-round pick for the Steelers coming out of Iowa last season.

Johnson ended up buried on Pittsburgh's dept chart, though, following the team's signings of Rico Dowdle and Travis Homer behind starter Jaylen Warren. As a rookie, the former All-American carried the ball just 28 times for 69 yards (2.5 yards per attempt) in the regular season, good for the third-most attempts on the team behind Warren and Kenneth Gainwell.

Funny enough, he was actually fourth on the Steelers in rushing yards last year, as tight end Jonnu Smith had nine carries for 70 yards and a touchdown. Smith, who previously played for head coach Matt LaFleur when LaFleur was an offensive coordinator for the Tennessee Titans, was signed by the Packers earlier this week.

Johnson played 11 snaps of special teams in 10 games, with 8 of those snaps being kickoff returns on which he got his hands on the ball. It doesn't seem like he has much of a background on teams other than as a kickoff returner, something that will probably go to receivers Skyy Moore and Savion Williams during the regular season. He had a long of 29 yards on his eight returns last year.

The Packers have released running back Pierre Strong Jr., according to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel's Tom Silverstein. It looks as though Green Bay will enter the regular season with four backs on its roster: Josh Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Johnson.

So far, there have been no reports on the compensation that the Steelers will receive for Johnson, be it a player or draft pick.

Update: NFL insider Adam Caplan is now reporting that the expected compensation for the Johnson trade is a future sixth-round pick.

#Packers are giving a 2028 sixth-round pick to the #Steelers for running back Kaleb Johnson, according to a source. The pick is their own and not the one they obtained from Miami.

So, the Packers functionally traded QB Kyle McCord for RB Kaleb Johnson.

It’s a 7th for Kaleb Johnson. Not a 6th. Even better! pic.twitter.com/iBp4Yat0Id

It is actually a seventh-round pick that was given up in the trade, not a sixth-round pick. This is interesting, since both the Packers and Steelers claimed it was a sixth-round pick, not a seventh-round pick. It's possible this is an error on the league's part.

title: Iowa State volleyball goes 2-1 at Cyclone Invitational
description: The Iowa State volleyball team experienced a rollercoaster of emotions during its season-opening tournament at Hilton Coliseum, finishing the three-day event with a pair of wins. After kicking off the campaign with a dominant sweep of Loyola Chicago on Friday, the Cyclones stumbled in straight sets against Georgia Tech on Saturday, before bouncing back Sunday […]
fullText:
The Iowa State volleyball team experienced a rollercoaster of emotions during its season-opening tournament at Hilton Coliseum, finishing the three-day event with a pair of wins.

After kicking off the campaign with a dominant sweep of Loyola Chicago on Friday, the Cyclones stumbled in straight sets against Georgia Tech on Saturday, before bouncing back Sunday with a thrilling, marathon four-set victory over in-state rival the University of Northern Iowa.

The Cyclones opened their 2026 campaign in style on Friday evening, dispatching Loyola Chicago in a swift 3-0 sweep (25-12, 25-20, 25-22) in front of 2,216 fans.

Iowa State's offense was highly efficient, registering a .277 hitting percentage with 40 kills and only 14 attack errors on 94 attempts. Nayeli Ti'a paced the Cyclones with a match-high 10 kills while hitting .333 and adding nine digs. Lilly Wachholz was equally effective, contributing nine kills on .300 hitting alongside five block assists. The Cyclones' defense, anchored by Rachel Van Gorp's 13 digs and Daaliyah Kemp's six total blocks (one solo, five assists), held the Ramblers to a meager .117 hitting percentage. Setter Ava Martin orchestrated the Iowa State offense beautifully, recording 33 assists, four digs, and two service aces.

Loyola Chicago (0-1) struggled to find its footing offensively, committing 18 errors on 94 total attacks. Leyna Nguyen led the Ramblers with nine kills but was plagued by five errors. Mallory Bohl was a bright spot for Loyola, slamming seven kills with just one error for an impressive .462 hitting clip. Setter Emma Henry dished out 13 assists in two sets of action, while Jae Fitting anchored the Ramblers' back row with nine digs.

On Saturday, the Cyclones faced a tougher challenge in Georgia Tech and were swept on their home court, falling 3-0 (25-23, 25-20, 25-17) before a crowd of 2,603.

The Yellow Jackets (2-0) showcased superior defensive pressure and offensive efficiency, hitting .229 as a team with 40 kills and 16 errors. Laura Perugini Bieleski was unstoppable for Georgia Tech, racking up 15 kills on a stellar .452 hitting percentage, while also adding six digs and two blocks. Alida Bennour added eight kills and two service aces, while Zoe Humphrey controlled the net with seven kills and five block assists. Heloise Soares guided the Yellow Jacket attack with 32 assists and eight digs, while libero Mana Kaneko tallied 11 digs.

Iowa State (1-1) was plagued by errors, hitting a dismal .093 as a team with 33 kills and 23 errors on 108 attempts. Nayeli Ti'a was the lone Cyclone to reach double-digit kills with 12, but she committed seven errors on 32 swings. Daaliyah Kemp had six kills on .385 hitting, and Macie Lupkes added four kills with a highly efficient .667 percentage. Ava Martin finished with 28 assists and five digs, while Rachel Van Gorp collected 11 digs.

The Cyclones closed out the tournament on Sunday with a classic battle against UNI, emerging victorious 3-1 (25-18, 25-18, 21-25, 36-34) in front of an energetic crowd of 3,207.

After cruising through the first two sets, the Cyclones dropped the third and were pushed to the absolute limit in an epic fourth set. The marathon frame featured 20 tie scores and seven lead changes before Iowa State finally secured the match with an extraordinary 36-34 set victory.

Iowa State's offense was firing on all cylinders, hitting .324 as a team with 66 kills on 142 total attacks. Nayeli Gonzalez was sensational in her season debut, carrying the Cyclones with 26 kills on a blistering .408 hitting clip, while adding eight digs and three block assists. Nayeli Ti'a delivered another powerhouse performance, registering 22 kills on .349 hitting with two aces.

Ava Martin posted a stellar double-double, dishing out a match-high 54 assists and digging up 10 balls. Rachel Van Gorp was a defensive wall, compiling a weekend-high 27 digs and adding two service aces. At the net, Lilly Wachholz added seven kills and five blocks, while Macie Lupkes led the blocking effort with seven block assists.

UNI (1-2) put up a fierce fight, led by an extraordinary performance from Cassidy Hartman. Hartman carried the Panthers with a match-high 27 kills on 69 swings, adding 10 digs and two service aces for a total of 30 points. Isabelle Elliott added eight kills, and Claire Munch chipped in seven. Setter Reese Booth finished with a double-double, registering 37 assists and 11 digs, while Jadyn Petersen led the Panthers' defense with 18 digs.

title: Steelers Make Eye-Opening Joey Porter Jr. Decision Amid Contract Standoff
description: The Pittsburgh Steelers made a big move involving star cornerback Joey Porter Jr., as the two sides remain in a standoff when it comes to their contract extension negotiations. The post Steelers Make Eye-Opening Joey Porter Jr. Decision Amid Contract Standoff appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have trimmed their roster down to 53 players ahead of the 2026 campaign, the final step standing between them and the start of the regular season. There were some surprising decisions as part of the team's roster cuts, but for the most part, the Steelers are riding into the new year with the crop of players that many folks were expecting them to have at their disposal.

One guy who wasn't exactly on the roster bubble, but whose status was still up in the air, was star cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Amid ongoing contract negotiations, Porter spent most of training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform list with a back injury. While no new deal has been reached here, that didn't stop Pittsburgh from making a move involving Porter on Sunday.

While the Steelers actually selected Porter with the No. 32 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, he was actually the first selection in the second round of the draft. That didn't figure to be much of an issue at the time, but it has actually played a surprising role in Porter's ongoing contract negotiations with Pittsburgh.

Since he wasn't a first-round pick, that means Porter's rookie contract didn't come with a fifth-year option, which the front office would have obviously exercised this offseason. Instead, Porter is entering the final year of his rookie deal, and he hasn't been shy in expressing his desire to receive a contract extension. The Steelers have been open to giving Porter a new deal, but there is a wide gap between the two sides in terms of his compensation.

As a result of these ongoing negotiations, Porter landed on the PUP list with a back injury, with some folks simply believing he wouldn't have practiced regardless due to his contract situation. If that was the case, it was a shrewd move to open up another roster spot, but now that the regular season is here, Pittsburgh needs Porter on the field. Even with his contract saga still hovering over the team, the Steelers have activated Porter off the PUP list ahead of the start of the regular season.

Activated off Active/Physically Unable to Perform: DB Joey Porter Jr.," the Steelers announced on their official website.

Porter has been a star corner for the Steelers since entering the pros, which is why settling his contract situation is so important. Last season, Porter racked up 52 tackles, 14 pass breakups, and one sack in 14 games of action, all of which were starts. Even though he didn't practice at all during training camp, Pittsburgh is counting on Porter to open the season as their top cornerback.

Whether or not he will be ready to go by the time Week 1 rolls around, though, is still unknown. While his back injury isn't expected to hold him out for four games (which is what would have happened had he stayed on the PUP list), there's no guarantee he can get himself up to speed in time for the season opener. Porter getting activated to the active roster is a big move, but his status still bears watching over the next couple of weeks.
