title: Winnipeg Jets Must Consider Major Factor in Connor Hellebuyck Trade
description: Unless interest in the Eastern Conference collapses, it's clear the Jets must complete a Connor Hellebuyck trade with a team that won't keep them out of a potential playoff competition next season. The post Winnipeg Jets Must Consider Major Factor in Connor Hellebuyck Trade appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
It's now painfully obvious that Connor Hellebuyck won't finish his career in Winnipeg. The likely future Hall of Fame goaltender has a full No Movement Clause in his contract, but that won't stop a Connor Hellebuyck trade from coming to fruition. In fact, multiple teams likely can begin looking at trade packages. As Chris Johnston of TSN and The Athletic notes, the Jets netminder has shown greater willingness to waive his trade protection than other notable trade-minded stars.

There are other factors, however, that will slow it down. According to Johnston, return is the primary factor. There's likely another one hidden and lurking. Preventing a Connor Hellebuyck trade from coming to fruition is the state of the Jets both on and off the ice.

One key difference with the Connor Hellebuyck trade request compared to others around the NHL is that he’s willing to waive his NMC for a variety of teams.

The offers haven’t been to Winnipeg’s liking just yet, obviously, but they’re not totally handcuffed.

— Chris Johnston (@reporterchris) August 28, 2026

https://platform.x.com/widgets.js

This isn't just about winning the trade on value. Winnipeg has to figure out how far back a Hellebuyck trade will set them.

At the time, Buffalo Sabres ownership reportedly had no interest in sending Eichel to the New York Rangers. The Sabres intended to basically charge the Rangers extra for Eichel, seemingly concerned about the optics of the franchise player winning with the 'big brother' of the tri-state area.

Now, the factors at play here are slightly different. First, the Jets are not in a clear-cut rebuild like Buffalo was at the time. Second, Winnipeg isn't purely worried about the optics. That's the critical point here. The Jets need to win this trade because the future of pro hockey in Winnipeg is riding on it. In the past few years, the Jets' ownership structure has publicly acknowledged some concerns. The Athletic reported in 2024 that the Jets were 'sounding the alarm' on their attendance concerns.

Surprisingly, those concerns emerged in the midst of a 110-point season. The next season, the Jets won the Presidents' Trophy in a 116-point season in 2025-26. They also won a playoff round, though Jets fans likely imagined they'd have advanced deeper that year. It's not clear if that fully allayed ownership's concerns. Still, the Jets did see a year-over-year boost in tickets reported in 2025.

Then last year happened, and the Jets collapsed. For the second time in five seasons, the Jets were basically non-competitive following multiple playoff berths. This failure was even more alarming, considering the 34-point year-over-year drop for a franchise that already has the second-smallest capacity of any NHL arena. That failure, which saw the Jets struggle almost everywhere, has directly led to a potential Connor Hellebuyck trade.

So now the Jets have to ask a simple question: can they take the best deal available? Conversely, is it more important to get Hellebuyck out of the Western Conference so they don't have to directly compete against him? This is less about optics and more about something hockey fans might have some sympathy for — figuring out how to compete for a playoff spot while simultaneously making the team worse and a Western Conference foe better.

Carolina, New Jersey, Pittsburgh, Washington, Buffalo, Detroit, Florida, Montreal, Ottawa and Toronto all have good reasons to explore a Connor Hellebuyck trade. That doesn't mean that all of them could pull off a potential deal. Toronto, Ottawa and Florida all recently committed to big-money goaltenders. The former two would likely want to move their respective netminders. Both Sergei Bobrovsky and Linus Ullmark have full No Movement Clauses. Florida has more flexibility, but the Panthers have few assets remaining to win a bidding war.

Montreal, Detroit and Buffalo all have good reason to get interested. These are teams with big prospect pipelines and the ability to send a goalie back the other way in a potential trade. While the Habs just committed to a Jakub Dobes contract extension, it has not kicked in yet. They could pair Hellebuyck with Jacob Fowler, one of the best goaltending prospects on the planet. Detroit could also have interest if such a move could be used to convince Dylan Larkin to rescind his trade request. The Sabres' interest is obvious, particularly after poor goaltending ended their first playoff run in 15 years.

The Metropolitan Division is murkier. Washington, clearly all-in on their own last dance with Alex Ovechkin, could be enticed to get involved. It would be complicated with the Capitals' salary cap situation. Carolina let Freddie Andersen walk, but it's hard to know if they'd increase their offer from earlier this summer. New Jersey's three-goalie tandem doesn't look ideal. However, there would be numerous other factors at play for New Jersey, including the status of Quinn Hughes. Kyle Dubas appears interested in bringing a big star to Pittsburgh. That said, Hellebuyck, 33, might be a little on the older side for them.

If there's enough interest out east, this won't matter. Still, it's plausible that no one in the Eastern Conference might step up for a Connor Hellebuyck trade. In the meantime, the list of suitors out west could include everyone but Vancouver, Calgary, Nashville and Dallas. Now, that doesn't mean they can all do it. For some teams, the interest is likely going to be soft. St. Louis might inquire about the price, but Joel Hofer might be a potential rising star. As a result, the Blues wouldn't be motivated. Anaheim, similarly, isn't likely to be very motivated, particularly while the cap situation there is a problem.

Colorado could build a trade around Mackenzie Blackwood but not much else. Similarly, Minnesota is already asset-depleted following the Quinn Hughes trade. Sure, they could build something around one of their two goaltenders, but it likely won't be enough. Los Angeles, Edmonton and Vegas are likely all interested and motivated. None of them likely have the goods to make such a move.

Chicago, Utah, San Jose and Seattle are likely the four best fits. Two of those teams will play Winnipeg four times per season, and the other two will play them three times per season. The Jets would directly compete for a playoff spot against Utah and Chicago in the Central, while simultaneously looking at wildcard spots against the other two.

The Jets are not rebuilding. It's not clear, even if ownership were to sign off on a rebuild, that it would be their best path forward. The Central Division is difficult, certainly. Still, there's volatility in Minnesota as long as the Quinn Hughes situation lingers. Utah looks poised to take a big step and join the division's big boys like Colorado and Dallas. Admittedly, those two might both have taken a step back this offseason. St. Louis has potential. However, the Blues have lacked consistency.

That does leave a path for Winnipeg to at least be competitive in the division, ideally still able to draw fans in as a result. Unless interest in the Eastern Conference collapses, it's clear the Jets must complete a Connor Hellebuyck trade with a team that won't keep them out of a potential playoff competition next season.

title: NFL Cutdowns: Former Packers pre-draft visitors released on Sunday
description: The Panthers waived linebacker Trevin Wallace, who was a starter for them last year, on Sunday
fullText:
I'll keep this one short: The Green Bay Packers target their pre-draft visitors at a high clip, whether it's the draft, as initial undrafted free agents or further down the line. For example, last cutdown cycle the team traded a pick for offensive linemen Darian Kinnard and picked up tight end Josh Whyle to the practice squad. Whyle eventually ended up winning a roster spot and made this year's initial 53-man roster.

So, who was just made available to the Packers? Good question. So far, these are the players who just hit the market and were brought to Green Bay during their draft cycle (since 2022, when the team started targeting more draft picks).

Can I interest anyone in Sean Clifford as a QB3 again?

The one I'm most interested here is rookie Damon Bankston, who received eight times the guarantees to sign with the New York Giants than the Packers' UDFA signing Jaden Nixon got this cycle. If Green Bay is pivoting to a more outside zone-based scheme, which has been the indication, I think Bankston fits really well. With that being said, he would probably be a practice squad signing immediately, not a 53-man roster guy.

I don't think the team wants to go down the Samori Toure path again, but rookie receiver Anthony Smith is interesting. Smith was taken two picks after Packers kicker Trey Smack. The seventh-round pick did not make it on the Dallas Cowboys' roster. He ran a 4.45-second 40-yard dash at 6'2" and 197 pounds.

Both Kiran Amegadjie and Esa Pole are players I could see the Packers adding to the bottom of their offensive line unit. Amegadjie was a third-round pick out of Yale for the Chicago Bears back in 2024, but he never caught on with the team. Esa Pola is a second-year former UDFA who was working with the first-team unit as the team's left tackle in Kansas City at points this summer, but the Chiefs traded for Diego Pounds right before the cutdown deadline.

With seven interior defensive linemen on the 53-man roster, I'm not sure the Packers even need a practice squad defensive lineman right now.

Sam Williams was arrested for felony sexual battery at Ole Miss, but the charges were later dropped. I know now this isn't a great time to say this, but the Packers bring in a lot of prospects with "off-field" red flags for visits, and they generally do it to rule them out completely. I do not expect Williams to be on Green Bay's short list.

Here's an interesting one: Trevin Wallace, the 2024 third-rounder who made 12 starts in 12 games played last year for the Carolina Panthers, was waived by the Panthers today. In total, he played 25 games (20 starts) for Carolina over two regular seasons. I could see the team taking a swing on him.

D'Arco Perkins-McAllister, Chiefs

D'Arco Perkins-McAllister actually started his college career off as a fairly big recruit, but wound up bouncing around schools after two years at TCU. He ended up at New Mexico, UT-Chattanooga and Louisiana-Monroe after that. He was waived by the Kansas City Chiefs, and it's not like the Packers' third-team defensive backs played well in the preseason. Maybe they change things up.

Safety is a position that will probably be more impacted on the practice squad level, if anything, than on the 53-man roster level, but two were made available today. Chris Edmonds has played almost exclusively as a special teamer when he's been active in NFL games in his career, while Jammie Robinson, a former fifth-round pick, is looking to catch on with his sixth team in four years. He's been available before, and the Packers haven't added him, so I'm not sure the 25-year-old is going to be a priority for them now.

title: Lions Announce Fates Of Injured Kerby Joseph, Brian Branch
description: Throughout training camp and the preseason, the Detroit Lions have been without safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles), who both remained on the PUP list.Now, with the regular season approaching, the Lions have provided a clearer outlook on the status of both players.According to the Lions, Joseph and Branch will begin the season […] The post Lions Announce Fates Of Injured Kerby Joseph, Brian Branch appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Throughout training camp and the preseason, the Detroit Lions have been without safeties Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles), who both remained on the PUP list.

Now, with the regular season approaching, the Lions have provided a clearer outlook on the status of both players.

According to the Lions, Joseph and Branch will begin the season on the PUP list, meaning both will miss at least the first four games of the 2026 campaign.

Last season, Joseph and Branch combined to miss 15 games last season due to injuries. Joseph was sidelined by a lower-body issue that ultimately ended his season after Week 6, while Branch suffered a torn Achilles against the Dallas Cowboys in December that also brought his season to an early close.

Earlier this month at the start of Training Camp, Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that Joseph was progressing in his rehab but was on a similar timeline to that of Branch, hinting that expected both players to miss the start of the season.

"Well, Kerby right now, first of all, he's dealing with a personal issue," Campbell said. "But, his rehab is coming along very well. OK, so I still see him on the (Brian) Branch plan if that makes sense. And Branch is doing well, too. So, those guys, we're talking about on down the road, the season's already begun, but I like where Kerby's at."

Not long after the 2026 NFL Draft in which the Lions did not select a safety, general manager Brad Holmes offered a somewhat optimistic health outlook for both Joseph and Branch.

"It wasn't that we intentionally didn't draft a safety because we feel good about them (Joseph and Branch). I feel like they're both trending in the right direction, but it just didn't line up," Holmes said. "Just like it hasn't lined up at other positions in the past, we didn't ignore it. There were some good ones that were out there that just got picked before we were able to, but it just didn't quite line up. I didn't really think that class was as deep either, so it had to line up and you had to strike right."

title: Eagles cut draft pick they loved last year
description: The Eagles waive young talent they liked last year.
fullText:
The Eagles have waived second-year offensive tackle Cameron Williams, one of many first and second-year players who were waived from the last two draft classes.

It's not surprising that Williams didn't make the roster this year. He struggled during the summer and did not show major signs of progression. His lack of development and growth is a disappointing result for the Eagles.

When the Eagles drafted Williams in the sixth round last year, they loved his potential.

"I think that you talk about a guy like Cam and you've got to look at it like, 'If this guy went back into school, where would he be a year from now?" Eagles general manager Howie Roseman said after the 2025 NFL Draft. "Where can we get this guy two years from now? What would that look like?'"

Williams slipped to Day 3 of the 2025 draft, but he was considered a Day 2 talent who needed to clean up consistency issues.

Last year, Williams missed the entire season with a shoulder injury up to Week 18. He started that game against the Washington Commanders and held his own. The future looked encouraging.

But in his second summer with the Eagles, Williams did not build off that momentum. He has great size (6-foot-5 and 317 pounds) and athleticism, but his lack of consistency is still an issue.

Even though Williams has failed to maximize his potential, the Eagles could still be interested in bringing him back on the practice squad.

The Rams cut their NFL roster to 53 players on Sunday after the preseason. Los Angeles waived defensive tackle Jaxson Moi.

title: 9 winners and 4 losers from the initial Bengals 53-man roster
description: Here are some winners and losers when it comes to the first version of the Bengals’ final roster.
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bengals have made their cuts and released the first version of their final roster on Sunday. They cut down from around 90 players to the 53 that will hopefully win the Bengals their first Super Bowl.

Of course, the Bengals will take a look at who was cut by the other 31 teams, and odds are they could put in a waiver claim or two. Until that happens, though, here are some winners and losers from the Bengals' initial 53-man roster.

There might not be a cooler story this season than Meyers'. From getting no D1 offers out of high school and having to pay $100 to try out for a CFL team to making a 53-man roster at 26 years old is the kind of stuff they make movies about. Meyers earned his spot too, catching 11 passes on 13 targets for 121 yards. He led the team in receptions and receiving yards this preseason, and will now take his spot on the most talented wide receiver corps in the NFL.

You know those guys that you can't help but like? You know, the ones that usually play for other teams that you always think, "Man, I wish that guy was a Bengal." Robinson is officially that guy. The seventh-round pick had a multi-sack preseason and not only made the Bengals' initial 53-man roster, but he appears primed to get some playing time early.

Stewart is a winner because, despite a nasty-looking hyperextension of his knee at the start of training camp, he won't be joining Brian Parker II and Ja'Sir Taylor on IR. That doesn't mean he's going to be ready to go by Week 1 (though it's not out of the realm of possibility), but it means he 'should' be good to go before Week 5, when he would have been eligible to come off IR.

Though Newton looked solid on Friday night against the Eagles in the Bengals' third preseason game, he struggled through much of camp and was reportedly in the doghouse. It appeared as if he was on route to getting cut, but thanks to Ja'Sir Taylor being placed on IR (with designation to return) due to a hamstring injury. This opened the door for Newton to stick around.

For now. These next four weeks are crucial for Newton's chances of remaining on the roster. Play well, and he may very well remain there for the rest of 2026.

The Bengals' starting offensive line is set, and has been set since before the offseason even began. Rivers is one of four backup offensive linemen to make the first version of the Bengals' final roster, but he wouldn't be if it weren't for the fact that Brian Parker II got placed on IR with Taylor with a knee injury.

Maybe the Bengals find a new offensive lineman from the many that are being cut throughout the league, but for now Rivers is on the roster.

This was likely the biggest surprise addition to the Bengals' 53-man roster. I would have thought Charlie Jones or Mitchell Tinsley would have the inside spot, but it was Williams who is the team's WR6 and likely kick and punt returner.

PFF gave him a score of 65.0 for kick returning and a 62.8 for punt returning compared to Jones' 67.5 and 69.8, but he also caught seven passes to Jones' four and Tinsley's three.

Brooks, the team's third running back, didn't do a lot to inspire confidence that, if the Bengals were to lean on him, he would be able to move the ball down the field. He only averaged 3.8 yards per carry on his 13 total rushing attempts.

Kentrel Bullock and Jamal Haynes never really had much of a chance at cracking the 53-man roster, but it wasn't for lack of trying. They both averaged more yards per carry, and both looked pretty solid on Friday night in Philly.

That, and the Bengals were reportedly interested in Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson. But once Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list, the Packers got desperate enough to trade for Johnson.

So for the time being, Brooks doesn't have any real competition for his spot.

Speaking of a lack of competition…

Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter

Knight and Carter continue to have a stranglehold on their jobs after the Bengals opted to keep just two other linebackers on the roster in Oren Burks and Swayze Bozeman, neither of whom looks capable of pushing for a starting spot.

Unless the Bengals make a trade or sign someone like Bobby Wagner, Knight and Carter are the starting linebackers for the foreseeable future. Let's hope they're ready to make a big jump from last year.

Jones and Tinsley were on the outside looking in when all was said and done on Sunday. Jones, a fourth-round pick in 2023, has been a solid return specialist in his time in Cincinnati, and Tinsley was one of the fun and exciting stories of the 2025 season.

Unfortunately, they were outshone by the trio of Williams, Colbie Young, and Meyers.

Taylor is on IR, but that's not why he's on the losers list. He's on this list because the four weeks he'll miss could be the four weeks Newton needs to prove he does belong on the final roster and hold on to his spot — whether that be on the field on defense or on special teams.

Taylor was signed in free agency on a one-year deal, and he was placed on IR with a designation to return. That return, at the earliest, would be in Week 5.

Newton, on the other hand, is a former fifth-round draft pick of the Bengals who is under contract through 2027. In other words, there's more incentive for the front office to keep Newton if this is a close battle.

Jackson struggled to get on the field in 2025, but the additions of Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen really sealed his fate. Now that fate is official. The 2024 third-round pick is now going to the practice squad or will be playing elsewhere.

title: “I Just Don’t Think Florida State’s Team is That Good”: CFB Analyst Rips Seminoles After Week 0 Win
description: The 2026 Florida State Seminoles are in an intriguing position. After a pair of seasons missing the College Football Playoff, they are looking to get back to the success they had a few years ago. With a Week 0 win already in their pocket as they attempt to get back into a bowl game, there […] The post “I Just Don’t Think Florida State’s Team is That Good”: CFB Analyst Rips Seminoles After Week 0 Win appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
The 2026 Florida State Seminoles are in an intriguing position. After a pair of seasons missing the College Football Playoff, they are looking to get back to the success they had a few years ago. With a Week 0 win already in their pocket as they attempt to get back into a bowl game, there are some people who are not believing in them this season. Let's take a closer look at one college football analyst who isn't buying the Seminoles this season.

While on Josh Pate's College Football Show, Pate made it known that he did not like what he saw from the Florida State Seminoles in their 34-17 Week 0 victory over New Mexico State.

"If you watched the game like I did, what was most alarming is just how evenly matched the teams looked for a lot of the night. The better team won here. Florida State is a superior team. I thought it would be end first quarter, 21-0. Go to half, 42-3. I expected that because there won't be a lot of those opportunities this year for Florida State. So I expected it, and it didn't happen, and I don't think because somebody was overlooking someone. I just don't think Florida State's team is that good."

The schedule will get tougher than playing New Mexico State. Pate explained how the schedule is not favorable for Florida State this year.

"Playing SMU and then in Tuscaloosa and then home for Virginia and then at Louisville, at Miami, and Clemson by Halloween is a recipe for disaster."

After a pair of bad seasons with a combined record of 7-17, Seminoles coach Mike Norvell cannot afford to be out of the College Football Playoff picture that early into the season. Even with a tough schedule, the Seminoles are hoping to make some noise in the ACC and get into the 12-team playoff. It will be intriguing to see how this program looks, as they were able to get some rust off against an inferior opponent.

title: Bruins’ McAvoy, Swayman Land Side-by-Side in NHL’s Top 50
description: Charlie McAvoy and Jeremy Swayman are among the best at their positions, and the NHL Network has them side-by-side in […]
fullText:
Charlie McAvoy and Jeremy Swayman are among the best at their positions, and the NHL Network has them side-by-side in its league-wide rankings.

On Sunday night, the NHL Network revealed the first 10 names on its Top 50 Players Right Now list, starting with No. 50 and finishing with No. 41. Two Boston Bruins landed on the first part of the list, with Jeremy Swayman ranked 42nd and Charlie McAvoy in front of him at No. 41.

Olympic gold medalist Charlie McAvoy is #️⃣4️⃣1️⃣ on NHL Network's Top 50 Players Right Now list!

📺: #NHLTopPlayers on NHL Network pic.twitter.com/GQZDxwNOWd

McAvoy, who ranked No. 38 in last year's list, fell back three spots after posting career highs in assists (50) and points (61). His slight drop did not lead to much criticism from NHL Network analysts Tony Luftman, Mike Rupp, and Mike Johnson, who were full of praise for McAvoy during Sunday night's reveal show.

"He's so unique because he does everything well. He does everything well, and some of the things that some players do well, like, I don't know, get 50 assists as a defenseman, generally aren't physically imposing. He is," Rupp said. "What do you need? He plays through injuries; we've seen that. He's nuts. The absolute warrior that he is."

"The only thing, for me, that from watching Charlie McAvoy, sometimes gets him in trouble, [is] because he cares too much," Rupp added. "Sometimes he tries to do a little bit too much. When he just goes and plays his game, he is a difference maker."

Even if Rupp believes McAvoy tries to do too much, he does everything for the Bruins. He averaged 24:23 of ice time per night last season, and he has led the Bruins in that category in seven of the last eight seasons. There has never been a year where McAvoy has averaged less than 22 minutes of ice time per night. He also punches in minutes on both the power play and penalty kill, and finished the 2025-26 season with a career-high 23 power play points (2-21–23).

"Underrated offensively. You think about Charlie McAvoy, I think people's first thought goes to all the stuff. The physical play, the defense, the leadership, the emotion, all that stuff," Mike Johnson said. "You're like, wait a second, 50 assists? That's a big, big number for a defenseman."

"He does it all for the Boston Bruins, and he also seems to represent the next person in the line of leadership, who the Boston Bruins want to be as a club […] He's the guy who plays hard, he's physical, he's in your face, he's the kind of player that the Bruins fans want to get behind and the Bruins organization wants to represent them."

There may not be one specific part of McAvoy's game that defines him, and Mike Johnson believes that's exactly what separates him from other defensemen in the league.

"If you want to talk about the best all-around guys, who can bring it [on] both ends, he's one of the best in the world."

Also Read:After Career-High Season, Charlie McAvoy Still Ranks 11th Among NHL Defensemen

Jeremy Swayman (@NHLBruins) is the first goaltender to appear on this year's Top 50 Players Right Now list!

📺: #NHLTopPlayers on NHL Network pic.twitter.com/6eYSYU2MR5

Jeremy Swayman did not rank in the top 50 last season, but landed at No. 49 entering the 2024-25 season. He's back on the list after a bounce-back season, and he was the first goaltender revealed in the top 50.

Swayman finished the year with 31 wins, topping his previous career-high of 25. He posted a .908 save percentage and a 2.71 goals against average, but he led the league in games started with a save percentage above .900 with 38. His third-place finish in Vezina Trophy voting only hints at how impactful he was to the Bruins last season, and how much of a role he played in helping the black and gold get back into the postseason.

"[The Bruins] were really driven by their great goalie. And Jeremy Swayman, you can talk about the goals saved above expected; you look at the traditional numbers here, [shows] how impactful he was on their team's success," NHL Network analyst Mike Johnson said. "This is what a great goalie can do. They can take an average team and make them an above-average team, and that's really what he did last year for Boston."

According to MoneyPuck, Swayman finished with 28.8 goals saved above expected, second to Washington's Logan Thompson. That marked a 37.9-goal improvement from the 2024-25 season, when he finished with a minus-9.1 GSAx.

"When you're talking about goals saved above expected, generally speaking, since we started tracking this, it comes from teams that don't really defend well, because that shows that the goaltenders are seeing stuff they probably shouldn't see," Mike Rupp said on the reveal show. "It's not always that case, but when you see this situation, Boston, if they can't improve the defensive game, get a little more predictable, he's shown that he could be a difference maker."

Just two weeks ago, the NHL ranked Swayman as the fifth-best goaltender in the league right now. Mike Rupp went on to call the position "one of the hardest, most polarizing positions in all of sports," and continued, saying that remaining consistent year over year is one of the toughest things to do as a goaltender.

title: Rutgers Finds Its Goals, Then Watches a Two-Goal Lead Disappear in 3-3 Draw With Providence
description: The Scarlet Knights scored twice in the opening 19 minutes and led by two with half an hour to play. Providence answered with three, the last two in 69 seconds.
fullText:
PISCATAWAY, N.J. — Seventeen days and three states after it opened the season in Knoxville, and three days after the weather took its home opener, Rutgers finally played a home game, and the goal drought that followed it up the coast ended barely two minutes in, but the clean sheet streak also ended in gutwrenching fashion. Providence drew Rutgers 3-3 on Sunday night at Yurcak Field, with the last two goals coming in the final minutes of the game.

Rutgers arrived at 0-1-2 with two clean sheets and 180 scoreless minutes behind it. Olivia Bodmer made six saves in the 0-0 draw at UConn and kept a second consecutive shutout at Fairfield, where Rutgers took the larger share of the shots and put too few of them on frame. The last Scarlet Knights goal came from Emma Johns in the 76th minute at Tennessee on Aug. 13, 17 days ago. With three goals in the game, Rutgers scored more than their previous three games combined, invoking a newfound hope in the attack.

Providence came to Piscataway unbeaten at 2-0-3, with three draws in five matches. The Friars opened 1-1 against UMass Lowell, beat Rhode Island 3-0, drew Monmouth, played out a scoreless 90 minutes at Northeastern and beat Stonehill 2-1 on Thursday. Freshman Jocy Koffi scored in each of the first two matches, including an 87th-minute equalizer against Lowell, and took BIG EAST Rookie of the Week; junior defender Stephanie Schoeley was named Defensive Player of the Week the same day. They went 6-6-4 last season, 3-4-3 in the Big East, and was picked sixth in the conference preseason coaches' poll. This clearly showed given their fight near the end of the game

GK: Olivia Bodmer
D: Julia Joseph, Morgan Hippeli, Lindsey Hailey, Jayme Malanda
M: Gabriela Gil, Lily Ann Phillips
F: Lilia Calvert, Reilly McGlinn, Ashley Baran, Amanda Thornton
Subs: Tommi Valente, Olivia Russomanno, Marian Dunne, Emma Johns, Sophia Stiles, Audrey Cain, Madelyn O'Neill, Riley Morris, Bea Tinoco

Mike O'Neill made one change to the XI that started at Fairfield, and it came in the back four. Jayme Malanda, who did not appear in the Fairfield box score at all, started at Providence. Patricia Tsokos, who had started each of the first three matches, does not appear in this one, not in the XI, not among the nine substitutes, no minutes logged.

That is now three consecutive weeks in which a Rutgers player has moved in or out of the matchday squad without explanation. Everything else held: Bodmer in goal, Gil and Phillips paired centrally, Calvert and Thornton keeping their places up front for a fourth straight start.

O'Neill used nine substitutes for a fourth straight match, and again emptied the bench before halftime. Then he did something he had not done all season, he put the entire starting XI back on the field for the second half. All eleven who kicked off restarted the match.

Gabriela Gil found Ashley Baran at 1:43 and Rutgers led before Providence had settled into the match at all. Amanda Thornton nearly doubled it 27 seconds later, dragging a shot right of the frame, and for a moment it looked like the kind of opening that decides a game early.

Providence did not let it. Signe Tingager forced Bodmer into a save at 2:46, Hinkle did the same 18 seconds later, and the Friars won corners at 3:11 and 6:16 as Rutgers spent the first ten minutes defending its own box. Hinkle struck the woodwork at 9:58. Meg Roden made Bodmer work again at 11:09. Tingager tested her a second time at 17:50, low to the left. Providence was chasing the game and playing like it, and the pressure produced real chances rather than territory.

Rutgers helped them along. Bodmer misplayed one save that the Friars could not punish, and a loose Calvert pass out of the back handed Providence a look it did not finish. Neither mistake cost anything, but both were the kind that have cost this team before. Then Calvert delivered for Reilly McGlinn at 18:28, and Rutgers led 2-0 against the run of play as it looked from the stands.

The numbers say otherwise. Rutgers finished the half with eight shots to Providence's seven and led 3-2 on corners. The Friars generated urgency without generating an edge in either column. What separated the teams was the frame. Providence put five of its seven attempts on target and scored none of them. Rutgers put two on target and scored both. Maria Ravotti did not make a save in 45 minutes of work.

Providence responded to the second goal immediately, sending on Marryn Gruhn and Kaitlyn Brady at 18:28, and O'Neill began his own rotation at 24:47 with Tommi Valente and Marian Dunne. Koffi drew a save at 24:14 and then the half went quiet. Dunne shot at 31:03, Morgan Hippeli at 32:57, Olivia Russomanno wide at 33:45, Lily Gibbs wide at the other end at 34:38. Rutgers was flagged offside three times before the break and Providence once. Both benches kept emptying, and by 38:04 the two teams had made 13 substitutions between them.

Caitlin Daley replaced Ravotti at the break and was tested inside ten seconds, Koffi forcing Bodmer into a save at the other end on the first attack of the half. Koffi won a corner at 48:51 and then scored from it, the ball curling in without touching anyone on its way. It was her fifth of the season and the kind of goal that changes a match's temperature.

For a while it did not. Rutgers restored the two-goal cushion at 54:31 when a Providence clearance went into the Friars' own net, and Providence answered by changing seven players at once at 56:49. That group came out pressing, Caitlin Driscoll's shot at 57:26 was blocked and credited as a team save, Koffi drew another Bodmer stop at 57:57, Courtnee Pickles and Samantha Kolb both had looks inside 70 seconds, and then the Friars stopped shooting almost entirely. From 58:32 to 74:15, Providence did not register an attempt.

That stretch belonged to Rutgers. The Scarlet Knights took 16 shots in the second half and seven corners, and for half an hour they controlled the ball in a way they have not managed at any point this season. Dunne had four attempts off the bench. Baran drew a save from Daley at 63:31 and shot over at 63:40. Lindsey Hailey forced another save at 66:33, Emma Johns another at 67:56. Calvert struck the crossbar at 81:59 with a shot that looked in from the moment it left her foot.

Daley saved all five Rutgers attempts that reached her. The only goal she conceded in 45 minutes was the one Providence scored on itself.

The discipline went first. Kolb was booked at 75:37, Leila Anazagasty-Pursoo at 78:50, and then Hippeli at 80:03, withdrawn 29 seconds later. Julia Joseph was cautioned at 85:57. All four yellow cards in the match came inside the final 15 minutes. In between the last two, Kolb delivered a ball to Hinkle at 84:51 and the Buffalo transfer scored her first goal for Providence, a finish that went to video review and stood. Koffi equalized at 86:00.

A two-goal lead Rutgers had held for half an hour was gone inside a minute and change, and the Scarlet Knights could not get it back. Hippeli's shot at 88:59 was the last thing either team generated. Rutgers outshot Providence 24-18 and led 10-4 on corners. Providence put 13 of its 18 attempts on target and Rutgers seven of 24. Koffi alone hit the frame six times in six tries. Bodmer made nine saves and conceded three. No Rutgers player registered more than two shots on goal.

The result leaves Rutgers winless with three draws and a shot profile that reads better than the record. Four matches in, the Scarlet Knights have produced their most complete half of soccer and their worst 90 seconds, and both happened Sunday.

Providence moves to 2-0-4, a team that has now drawn four of six. Rutgers gets Princeton at Yurcak on Sunday before Big Ten play opens, with the Boston College makeup still unscheduled.

The goals came back. Holding them is the next thing.

title: 59 former Ohio State football players make final 53-man NFL rosters
description: Sunday was the day when NFL teams had to trim their rosters to the final 53-man opening day limit. There are a whopping 59 former Ohio State players.
fullText:
Sunday was the date on which NFL 53-man rosters had to be set, and we're always interested in which former Ohio State players make the cut and who gets left out in the cold, searching to continue their dreams in another way. As you would expect, there's a slew of scarlet and gray littered across NFL teams, and in fact, 59 former Buckeyes are officially on rosters across the League.

Of note, only five teams in the NFL do not have at least one former Ohio State player on their roster. And by former players, we are only considering those who finished their careers in scarlet and gray, not elsewhere. Only the Bengals, Chargers, Eagles, Packers, and Ravens don't have a former Buckeye on the roster. There would be an even 60 players if not for Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper being placed on the commissioner's exempt list because of two domestic violence charges. We'll follow where that news leads.

The Cleveland Browns and Arizona Cardinals lead all teams with six former Ohio State players each. As always, however, with the news of players making NFL rosters, some did not. Eight former Buckeyes were released from rosters on Sunday:

San Francisco 49ers: CB Eli Apple

Cincinnati Bengals: WR Xavier Johnson

Kansas City Chiefs: S Tanner McCalister, DE Tyreke Smith

Philadelphia Eagles: G Michael Jordan, CB Shaun Wade

Carolina Panthers: DT Tywone Malone Jr.

New Orleans Saints: RB CJ Donaldson Jr.

Pittsburgh Steelers: LB Malik Harrison

Tennessee Titans: DL Jalyn Holmes

Also interesting to note is the fact that two former Ohio State players who went undrafted beat the odds and made an NFL roster as undrafted free agents. Former center and Rimington Award winner Seth McLaughlin was retained by the Detroit Lions, while offensive lineman Josh Fryar made the cut for the Arizona Cardinals.

title: Eagles surprisingly waive both international rookies and risk losing them
description: Eagles waive two rookies.
fullText:
The Eagles waived seventh-round pick Uar Bernard and undrafted edge rusher Joshua Weru on Sunday night.

Bernard, from Nigeria, and Weru, from Kenya, were among the best stories during training camp. They had never played football prior to this season, but the Eagles took a chance on both players, and the early results were encouraging.

Especially with Weru. He finished with a sack against the Patriots and applied pressure in the other two preseason games. He is an exceptional athlete.

Bernard, a defensive tackle, is bigger a project than Weru. He struggled at times during the games, but it's still surprising to see him get waived. He's an elite athlete with absurd physical upside.

The Eagles took a risk waiving both players. They were both expected to make Philadelphia's 53-man roster to avoid losing them to another team.

NFL teams could claim both players on Monday afternoon off the waiver wire. Weru is more likely to be claimed because he showed more upside in the games.

Bernard is 6-foot-4 and 306 pounds with a body fat of 6%. He ran the 40-yard dash at his Pro Day in 4.63 seconds. Another NFL team could be bold enough to claim him off waivers if they believe in his long-term potential.

title: New York Jets 2026 practice squad tracker with news and live updates
description: The Jets have selected the players for their initial roster in 2026. The work is not finished, however. The team can now begin assembling its practice squad. NFL teams are allowed to assemble a 17 players practice squad. These players practice with the team and attend meetings through the week.
fullText:
The Jets have selected the players for their initial roster in 2026. The work is not finished, however.

The team can now begin assembling its practice squad. NFL teams are allowed to assemble a 17 players practice squad. These players practice with the team and attend meetings through the week. Every week, two players can be activated from the practice squad to play in games. These players do not need to be added to the active roster the first three times they are activated for a game. The fourth time, however, the team must add them to the 53 man roster.

Practice squad players are technically free agents and able to sign with the active roster of any team aside from upcoming opponents.

Who is eligible for the practice squad?

Teams can use up to 16 of their 17 slots on players with no NFL seasons or one season (with less than nine games played) if they so choose. For a fully stocked practice squad, the minimum number of players with this level of experience is 6.

Teams are also allowed to choose up to 10 practice squad players with more experience. No more than six can have more than two years of experience in the NFL.

Finally, one spot must go to an international player.

We will keep track of the players the Jets sign to the practice squad below.

title: Ex-Eagles QB traded to AFC team, hurting Philly’s trade market
description: Eagles QB trade update.
fullText:
The Eagles could look to trade Andy Dalton or Tanner McKee before the start of the season, but there are not many obvious trade partners.

One of the teams that made sense was the Miami Dolphins, given their need for a backup quarterback after trading Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Former Eagles offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo landed with Miami this offseason after getting fired by Philadelphia in January. McKee reuniting with Patullo would have made some sense, too.

That possibility no longer exists.

The Dolphins traded a sixth-round pick in 2028 to the Green Bay Packers for Kyle McCord, who was drafted by the Eagles in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. McCord was waived last summer after struggling during camp and spent the entire year on the Eagles' practice squad. He left the Eagles after the season to sign with the Packers and revived his career with a strong performance in his second training camp.

title: 6 stunning choices on the Lions’ initial 53-man roster
description: Here are five of the biggest shocks from the Detroit Lions’ initial 53-man roster.
fullText:
The Detroit Lions dropped their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season—see it here—and there were plenty of big surprises in their choices. Now, the Lions are likely to make some tweaks over the next 48 hours, so it's important not to overreact until they truly settle on a Week 1 roster.

But here are 6 shocking decisions the Lions front office made with this initial roster.

A few weeks ago, Dan Campbell noted that the RB4 competition between Jacob Saylors and Jabari Small was neck-and-neck. However, since then, it's been almost all Saylors. He finished the preseason with more scrimmage yards than any other player in the NFL, while Small failed to stay on the field. Small missed the first preseason game with an injury, left Game 2 with a concussion, and left Game 3 with another injury.

Yet the Lions liked enough of what they saw in Small to give him a coveted roster spot. That is perhaps the most shocking decision of all.

Not far behind was Detroit's decision to only keep four receivers. While everyone had Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa, and Tay Martin on their 53-man roster predictions, a fifth almost seemed necessary and certain.

Greg Dortch is a trusted veteran who looked great as a punt returner all August and had experience with offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. When it was revealed that Dortch was being released, it was certainly Tom Kennedy who won the spot, right? Nope, he was released in the final cuts as well.

So…. what is the Lions' plan at punt returner? Just a few weeks ago, special teams coordinator Dave Fipp said the competition was between Dortch and Kennedy. So, either one (or both) is coming back to the practice squad (or 53-man roster), or some unknown player on the roster will step up. But in all honesty, I don't have the faintest of clues who on the current roster could take over those duties.

Not many questioned whether Tyler Conklin's spot on the roster was in jeopardy. He frequently repped ahead of Jackson Meeks, and looked just fine in his role as TE3 behind Sam LaPorta and Brock Wright. For as many two- and three-tight end formations the Lions are expected to use, having an experienced veteran like Conklin seemed like a no-brainer—especially after the struggles they went through last year when LaPorta and Wright went down with injuries.

And while many of us had Meeks on the roster as TE4, trusting him as the team's TE3 is a risky move for a player who is still learning the nuances of the position. That said, Meeks earned it on special teams, and that's where his initial role will be.

One final thing to keep in mind: as a vested veteran, Conklin's salary would have been fully guaranteed if he was on the active roster in Week 1, and this could be their way of circumventing that rule. If they add him to the practice squad, they could elevate him in Week 1, then re-sign him to the active roster in Week 2.

EDGE Eric O'Neill: 6-foot-2, 250
EDGE Ahmed Hassanein: 6-foot-2, 275
DT Skyler Gill-Howard: 6-foot, 280
DT Mekhi Wingo: 6-foot, 282

These four players who made the 53 shined in the preseason predominantly because of their pass rush, while their abilities as run defenders are still a work in progress. Meanwhile, these players:

EDGE Anthony Lucas: 6-foot-5, 265
DT Chris Smith: 6-foot-1, 310
DT Ben Stille: 6-foot-4, 296

None of them made it. This represents a pretty clear shift in the preferences of their defensive linemen, with a newfound lean into getting to the quarterback.

That isn't to say they don't have size on the roster. Alim McNeill (6-foot-2, 310), Tyleik Williams (6-foot-3, 325), Levi Onwuzurike (6-foot-3, 304), and DJ Wonnum (6-foot-5, 262) are all big for their positions. But it appears they want some juice with their reserves.

Maybe not the biggest shock, considering Rolder himself told the media that he believes he's close to a return. But when the injury happened, it appeared the Lions' fourth-round rookie was going to miss significant time. Instead, the Lions believe his development is important enough to stay on the roster and avoid a four-week absence on IR.

Detroit had enough linebacker reserves that they would've been fine if Rolder went on IR, but they clearly believe in Rolder's health and ability to make a difference early this season.

Through a few weeks of training camp, there was no better story than Nick Whiteside. He had worked his way up from the bottom of the depth chart to sharing some first-team defense reps at cornerback. He played a physical style of game that seemed like a great fit.

And while he admittedly cooled down a bit toward the end of training camp, some of that was simply due to him having to cover the safety position that was plagued by injuries. I thought flashing that versatility would only strengthen his case for the 53-man roster. Instead, Detroit favored guys like Ennis Rakestraw, who has more potential, and Khalil Dorsey, who is one of the team's best special teamers.

title: Scottie Scheffler ends the longest run in PGA Tour's money game
description: Tiger Woods had been the PGA Tour's all-time earnings leader since 2000. Scottie Scheffler's Tour Championship win put him past the golf legend.
fullText:
Tiger Woods was 24 and going for his seventh straight win when he tied for second at Torrey Pines. The check was $264,000. It made him the PGA Tour's all-time money leader, which nobody really thought much about at the time. It was Feb. 13, 2000.

He never moved from atop that list. Even through the swing changes, the surgeries and the years he barely played at all.

Woods was the all-time earnings leader for over 26 years, until Sunday.

Scottie Scheffler took that title from him Sunday afternoon in Atlanta. It took him less than a decade.

Scheffler began the final round of the Tour Championship three shots behind, but passed Viktor Hovland on the back nine and won his second FedEx Cup. The win was worth $10 million and it moved him to $130,390,661 for his career. Woods sits at $120, 999,166.

Nobody is saying their careers are close.

Woods won 82 times and took 15 majors. Scheffler is 30 with 22 wins and four majors. But times have changed. Woods beat Davis Love III in a playoff in Las Vegas in 1996 for his first Tour title and he got a check worth $297,000. The man who finished last at East Lake on Sunday made $355,000.

But Woods took to social media to congratulate Scheffler on his 2026 season.

"Three wins, five runner-ups and finishing the season No. 1. Those are some numbers to be proud of. Incredible consistency all season long. Congrats on a historic season, Scottie," Woods wrote on X.com.

title: Another player involved in college eligibility suit gets cut by an NFL team
description: Defensive lineman Jack Pyburn was waived by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday and could be the latest player who tries to go back to college after spending time in an NFL camp.  Pyburn was among the cuts on the day NFL teams reduced their rosters to 53.
fullText:
Defensive lineman Jack Pyburn was waived by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday and could be the latest player who tries to go back to college after spending time in an NFL camp.

Pyburn was among the cuts on the day NFL teams reduced their rosters to 53. He could now try to get a fifth year of eligibility if he is not claimed on waivers by another team Monday. He'll become a free agent if he's not picked up and is among the players granted a temporary restraining order by a Louisiana court earlier this month that would make them eligible to return to college athletics. Pyburn's likely landing spot would be LSU.

Four other players who spent time on NFL rosters this offseason before being cut were also part of the case: former LSU running back TJ Harden, former Mississippi tight end Dae'Quan Wright, former Ole Miss defensive lineman Zxavian Harris and former Oregon State running back Anthony Hankerson.

These players all entered the NFL draft process because they had used up their four years of eligibility. The NCAA announced a rule change in June allowing players who began college in 2023 or later to have five years to play five seasons.

That rule didn't apply to these players because they entered college in 2022. They have sued the NCAA, arguing they're being deprived of education and potential name, image and likeness benefits by being excluded from the rule.

The Power Four conferences have all ruled that players who signed NFL contracts are ineligible to return to college, but those rules remain in legal limbo until court cases are resolved. The Southeastern Conference's rule is part of a court hearing scheduled for Thursday. SEC rosters become final Friday.

Under NFL rules, any player who returns to college for any time will be ineligible to play this season. Those players would become free agents who are free to sign with any team in 2027.

Here's a look at some of the players who spent time in NFL camps this summer and now might return to college:

Pyburn originally signed as an undrafted free agent with Tampa Bay in May. He played in two exhibition games and led the NFL with four sacks in the preseason. Pyburn played his first three college seasons at Florida and spent last season at LSU.

Harden signed as an undrafted free agent with Cleveland in May before getting waived Aug. 3. He then signed with Seattle three days later and appeared in one exhibition game, gaining 1 yard on two carries and recovering a fumbled punt. He was waived Aug. 17 by the Seahawks. Harden played three years in college at UCLA and finished last season at SMU. He rushed for 2,445 yards and 21 TDs in 44 career games.

Harden is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and is reportedly interested in playing for Missouri or Kentucky.

Wright originally signed as an undrafted free agent with Philadelphia in the spring but was waived by the Eagles on Aug. 10. He was claimed by Cleveland the next day and spent nearly two weeks with the Browns before getting waived again on Aug. 23. Wright didn't appear in a preseason game. Wright played his first two seasons in college at Virginia Tech and final two at Mississippi. He had 113 catches for 1,603 yards and five TDs in 47 career games.

Wright is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and wants to play for his former Ole Miss coach, Lane Kiffin, at LSU.

Harris originally signed as an undrafted free agent with New Orleans in May and began training camp with the Saints. He was waived on Aug. 8 before the first preseason game. Harris played four seasons in college at Ole Miss and had 5 1/2 sacks in 52 games. He had two of his career-high nine tackles for loss last season in the College Football Playoff.

Wright is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and also wants to play for Kiffin at LSU.

Hankerson originally signed as an undrafted free agent with Miami in the spring and began camp with the Dolphins. He was waived on Aug. 10 and signed a week later with Seattle. He spent one week with the Seahawks before getting waived again on Aug. 24. Hankerson had five carries for 10 yards and two catches for 9 yards for Seattle in an exhibition game against Tennessee on Aug. 23. Hankerson played his first two seasons in college at Colorado and the final two at Oregon State. He rushed for 2,761 yards and 28 TDs in 44 career games and had back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons for the Beavers.

Hankerson is part of the lawsuit in Louisiana and could try to return to Oregon State.

title: Aaron Judge to join Yankees on West Coast trip as rehab progression continues
description: NEW YORK — Aaron Judge is set to join the Yankees on this week’s West Coast road trip as he continues to work his way back from a broken rib. Judge has been progressing through baseball activities — including throwing from 100 feet and taking indoor, overhand batting practice — but had not yet faced high-velocity pitching. “I’m sure he’ll be ramped up and a lot more involved in the pregame ...
fullText:
NEW YORK — Aaron Judge is set to join the Yankees on this week's West Coast road trip as he continues to work his way back from a broken rib.

Judge has been progressing through baseball activities — including throwing from 100 feet and taking indoor, overhand batting practice — but had not yet faced high-velocity pitching.

"I'm sure he'll be ramped up and a lot more involved in the pregame stuff," manager Aaron Boone said Sunday of the plan for Judge on the road trip.

"Hopefully out there, [Judge will] start to get on velocity and things like that, be part of the pregame stuff, and just get more entrenched into getting ready to come back."

The Yankees are set to begin a three-game series against the Los Angeles Angels in Anaheim on Monday, then play the Padres in San Diego over the weekend.

They have not shared a timeline for Judge to return, but with the Yankees in the thick of a playoff race, the slugger said last week that he would prefer to forgo a minor-league rehab assignment.

"Why waste at-bats?" Judge, 34, said Thursday. "Why waste anything down in a minor-league game? I've been doing this for a while now, and I've got a sense of what I need to do on the field and how to manage it, so why waste at-bats in Double-A or Triple-A?"

Judge has been sidelined since May 31 due to a right rib stress fracture — an injury he suspects occurred more than a month earlier when he dove in right field during a game in Houston.

The three-time American League MVP is hitting .248 with 17 home runs and a .907 OPS in 59 games this season. In his absence, Spencer Jones and Heliot Ramos are sharing time in right field.

In 2023, Judge didn't play in any minor-league rehab games before returning from a toe injury that had kept him out for about two months.

There are four weeks remaining in the regular season.

"I'm gonna play smart," Judge said last week. "I'm gonna still try to go out there and make every play I can, but you gotta be smart, especially near the end of the year now. You know, if it's Game 7 of the World Series, I'll definitely be diving, so I don't think that'll ever change. But just be smart the next couple weeks as we get back, and we'll be good."

title: Broncos waive former Texas A&M LB, hope to add him to practice squad
description: Denver waived former Texas A&M LB Taurean York but hopes to bring him back on the practice squad if he clears waivers after a solid preseason showing.
fullText:
As roster churning continues across the NFL in the days following cut‑down day, teams that waived players they liked but couldn't fit on the initial 53‑man roster now have to wait and see whether those players clear waivers. Unlike vested veterans who become free agents immediately, waived players must pass through the waiver wire before the team that released them can re‑sign them to the practice squad.

For the Denver Broncos, that's the situation with former Texas A&M linebacker Taurean York, who was waived Sunday, per Chris Tomasson. York received a notable $25,000 signing bonus, the highest among Denver's undrafted free agents, signaling how much the organization valued bringing him into camp. He delivered a solid preseason, recording four tackles and flashing the instincts and competitiveness that defined his college career.

Making an NFL roster as an undrafted free agent is always a long shot. Roughly 15% of UDFAs make an initial 53‑man roster, and about 25% land on a practice squad. That means the majority never appear in a regular‑season game. For York, the Broncos have made it clear they want him back on the practice squad if he goes unclaimed.

York has always been an underdog, and this is simply the next test in a career built on proving doubters wrong. If he clears waivers, he'll have another opportunity to continue that journey in Denver.

Talked to Robert York, father of LB Taurean York. He said he talked to Taurean and #Broncos are waiving him but they want him on the practice squad. I had talked to Robert, a former player, in May for a big story on Taurean.

title: Metayer's rebound goal gives the Spirit a 1-0 victory over Bay FC
description: Paige Metayer scored on the rebound after Trinity Rodman's shot hit the crossbar to lift the Washington Spirit to a 1-0 victory over Bay FC on Sunday.  Rodman collected the ball just beyond Audi Field’s middle-third late in first-half stoppage time, drove to the corner of the 6-yard-box and struck the bottom of the crossbar.  Metayer crashed the goal line and knocked in the rebound before goalkeeper Jordan Silkowitz could react.
fullText:
Paige Metayer scored on the rebound after Trinity Rodman's shot hit the crossbar to lift the Washington Spirit to a 1-0 victory over Bay FC on Sunday.

In the day's later National Women's Soccer League match, the Seattle Reign slipped by the Houston Dash 1-0.

Rodman collected the ball just beyond Audi Field's middle-third late in first-half stoppage time, drove to the corner of the 6-yard-box and struck the bottom of the crossbar. Metayer crashed the goal line and knocked in the rebound before goalkeeper Jordan Silkowitz could react.

Rodman was later on the receiving end of a late tackle from Bay FC's Maddie Moreau, who earned a yellow card. Washington's Metayer and Gabrielle Carle were also given yellows.

Bay FC (6-11-4) kept pace with the Spirit (12-6-4), matching Washington's four shots on goal and keeping a slight edge in possession. Bay committed just five fouls to Washington's 10 as the injury-riddled Spirit secured its first victory in five matches.

Maddie Dahlien scored the sixth winner of her career at Lumen Field, breaking through in the 52nd minute to lift the Seattle Reign (10-8-4) past the Houston Dash (7-11-5).

She had a team-high five shots, four of those on target. Maddie Mercado provided the assist, sending a well-placed cross beyond the reach of goalkeeper Jane Campbell and into Dahlien's path.

Campbell made four saves, including a one-on-one stop against Dahlien in the 80th minute when she sprawled to deny the Reign forward on a counterattack.

Both teams will soon lose key players to the United States Under-20 women's national team, which will compete at the U-20 Women's World Cup in Poland. Seattle's Ainsley McCammon and Houston's Linda Ullmark are expected to join the squad in September before returning to their clubs.

title: Purple Row After Dark: What are you watching around MLB this September?
description: The Rockies may be struggling, but the rest of baseball is giving us plenty to watch.
fullText:
For most of the season, my attention stays pretty firmly on the Colorado Rockies.

That will not change down the stretch, but the losses are starting to stack up again. The Rockies are 4-11 over their last 15 games, and that can get frustrating.

Sometimes it is nice to look up and see what else is happening around baseball, and as the calendar nears September, it is a good time to do exactly that.

Fortunately, baseball's final month looks to hold plenty of intrigue, both in the standings and on individual leaderboards.

While not a particularly good division, the AL West might be the least settled division race of all. Houston sits at 69-68, just one game above .500. Texas is 67-70 and two games back, while Seattle sits at 64-73 and five games out. Houston does not exactly look interested in running away with the division, but Texas and Seattle have not shown much desire to take it from them, either. Personally, I would not mind a Houston-less October.

Then there are the White Sox. Two years removed from losing 121 games, Chicago is 72-64 and leads the 69-68 Guardians by 3.5 games in the AL Central. Can they finish off one of baseball's more unexpected division titles — or can the Rockies perhaps play spoilers in the final days of the season?

Both Wild Card races still leave room for a late surprise. Cleveland holds the final AL spot, but Baltimore is just one game back, Toronto is 1.5 out and Texas sits two back. In the NL, Arizona holds the final spot by just a half-game over San Diego, while Miami remains 3.5 games out.

Meanwhile, Yordan Alvarez enters the stretch run hitting .320 with 37 home runs and 93 RBI. He leads the American League in all three categories, putting a Triple Crown firmly within reach.

On the mound, Jacob Misiorowski owns a 1.73 ERA with 222 strikeouts in 151 innings. If he can stay below 2.00 and reach 250 strikeouts, he would be the first pitcher to accomplish both since Jacob deGrom in 2018.

And the National League home run race is of particular interest to us Rockies fans. Kyle Schwarber leads the league with 40, Matt Olson has 37, and Hunter Goodman is tied with Pete Crow-Armstrong at 36. Goodman has already produced two three-homer games this season, so we know he can hit them in bunches.

Those are a few things I will be watching.

What about you? What race, milestone, player or team has your attention as we head into September?

title: SEC’s fight to block former pros could decide how college football enforces rules
description: LSU commitments Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris have reignited the SEC's fight over whether former professional players can return to college football.
fullText:
The college football season got underway in Week 0, but off-field battles are still brewing. This time, an entire conference is fighting for the power to enforce its established rules regarding professional athletes returning to college athletics.

The SEC was told by a Baton Rouge, Louisiana, judge that the conference could not punish schools that sign former professional players. College football has done everything it can to draw a clear line between itself and professional sports.

Now, the SEC is getting ready to rumble. In court, of course. The SEC and Commissioner Greg Sankey will contest the ruling in court Thursday and are prepared to fight back.

MORE: College football analyst doubts Dae'Quan Wright will ever take the field for LSU

"The order entered against the SEC and Commissioner Sankey is a temporary restraining order, not a final ruling on the merits. The SEC and Commissioner Sankey are prepared to contest the allegations in the plaintiffs' petition at Thursday morning's hearing and defend the SEC's rights as a voluntary association to fulfill its mission to its member institutions." The SEC said in a statement via CBS Sports.

Jul 20, 2026; Tampa, FL, USA; SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey speaks to the press during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris have both committed to the LSU Tigers through the transfer portal. While Harris spent only a short time with the New Orleans Saints, Wright saw game action with the Cleveland Browns. The Browns claimed Wright off waivers on August 11 and he appeared in preseason games.

Harris did not appear in any preseason contests, but he and Wright both declared for the 2026 NFL Draft. They also went through the full draft process and became undrafted free agents. After yet another bizarre ruling, both players regained their college eligibility and decided to enter the transfer portal.

MORE: Can USC quarterback Jayden Maiava take Fernando Mendoza-like leap in 2026?

Both played at Ole Miss in 2025 under current LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin. In typical Kiffin fashion, he has been vocal in opposing the conference's efforts to prevent the two players from playing.

Jan 8, 2026; Glendale, AZ, USA; Mississippi Rebels tight end Dae'Quan Wright (8) scores a touchdown against the Miami Hurricanes during the 2026 Fiesta Bowl and semifinal game of the College Football Playoff at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The reality is that this has simply gone too far. When a player declares for the NFL Draft, that should undoubtedly end his college football career. Instead, we have reached a point where players are looking for a judge who will give them what they want.

There is no true merit to these rulings beyond arguments that are enough to get an injunction granted. The Brendan Sorsby case was just the beginning. If college sports cannot enforce their rules, what will be next?

The fate of this line in the sand could rest on the shoulders of the SEC.

title: 6 takeaways after Broncos set initial 53-man roster
description: The Broncos set their initial 53-man roster on Sunday. Here are six quick takeaways.
fullText:
The Denver Broncos had a busy weekend.

Denver's front office made 38 moves over the last two days to get down to an initial 53-man roster.

"Every year is hard, regardless of your depth," general manager George Paton said on Sunday evening. "This is a tough day. It's always challenging. This year, I think we spent more time on this roster going through a lot of different scenarios with a lot of these players that were released. It's a puzzle. It's ongoing. Now we're building the practice squad, we're looking at the wire tonight, obviously. So it's fluid, and yet yes, this was a tough roster to make."

With that noted, here are six quick takeaways from Paton's post-cuts conference call.

1. Broncos injury report: Offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo was moved from the active/physically unable to perform list to the reserve/PUP list, and tight end Caleb Lohner and offensive tackle Frank Crum were placed on short-term injured reserve. All three players will be eligible to return after four games, but they might not all be ready that quickly. Paton roughly estimated Lohner could return in October.

2. Justin Joly among cut draft picks: Denver cut three members of their 2026 NFL draft class: tight end Justin Joly (fifth round), linebacker Red Murdock (seventh round) and safety Miles Scott (seventh round). All three players will likely be top targets for the Broncos' practice squad — if they clear waivers. "You always worry about the guys you want to bring back that they could get claimed," Paton said. "If they do, like we told them, we're going to give them a hug and wish them the best. That's part of it; that's part of the league. It's a risk when you put guys out there. It's just part of it."

3. Sam Ehlinger returns as QB3: After not making the initial 53-man roster last summer, Ehlinger has made the active roster in 2026. "Sam is a big part of this quarterback room," Paton said. "We didn't want to lose him, and we felt we were going to lose him [if he was cut]. He's too important to our team and just didn't want to risk doing that. Obviously, the game he played the other night was outstanding. We love the room. We're going to keep the room together." Denver didn't want to take the risk of attempting to bump Ehlinger down to the practice squad because other clubs likely would have offered him a spot on their active roster.

4. Jaleel McLaughlin's moving on: After being waived on Sunday, this feels like the end of McLaughlin's time in Denver (he posted a goodbye message on Instagram). Paton said choosing between Tyler Badie and McLaughlin was one of the hardest and one of the final cut decisions the Broncos made. Paton noted that special teams and "third-down ability" were two key factors. Badie, unlike McLaughlin, is heavily involved in the kicking game, and he's a reliable pass blocker.

5. Broncos get roster flexibility with two cuts: Two of Denver's notable cuts were fullback Adam Prentice and long snapper Mitchell Fraboni. Because they are vested veterans, neither player is subject to the NFL's waiver wire. The Broncos plan to re-sign both players to their practice squad, and they can be elevated to the game-day roster up to three times. Eventually, Prentice and Fraboni will be fully promoted to the active roster. In the meantime, Denver has some early-season roster flexibility with those two on the practice squad.

6. Jonathon Cooper placed on exempt list: The NFL placed Cooper on the commissioner's exempt list on Sunday, which means he can't practice or play in games until the league makes an updated ruling. In the meantime, the Broncos still have Nik Bonitto, Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson and Dondrea Tillman at outside linebacker. Paton said Denver likes their OLB room, but he also acknowledged the team will look for depth. "[W]e'll be looking a little bit, looking on the practice squad and we'll be looking around," Paton said. "You can never have enough pass rushers, so we'll kind of see how that goes."

Up next are waiver claims on Monday morning. After claims are processed, the Broncos can begin building a 17-player practice squad for the 2026 NFL season (expect Prentice and Fraboni to be among the first signings).

title: 7 players on 49ers roster who could be headed for IR
description: The San Francisco 49ers have their initial 53-man roster, but now they'll make some additional moves to free up roster spots.
fullText:
Even after an avalanche of roster moves at Sunday's deadline for final cuts, the San Francisco 49ers still have plenty of work to do on their roster.

With a handful of players likely returning to the club in some capacity, the 49ers will need to free up some roster spots. They could do that via the outright release of someone who made the first version of the 53-man roster. They can also create roster spots by placing players from the 53-man group on IR. Players who are on the roster and then go on IR can be designated for return. Players who are placed on IR before final cuts can't return, save for the maximum two players who are allowed to be given return designations.

One key with the return designations that come down at final cuts is that they count toward the maximum eight IR returns for the season, even if they never come off IR. That forces teams to be strategic with how they utilize those IR slots on cutdown day.

Now that we know what the 49ers' initial 53-man roster looks like, and we know they'll need to clear up a couple of roster spots, here are seven players who could be tagged for IR now that they've made the initial roster:

Lowe suffered a high ankle sprain early in camp. There's a chance he'll be ready for the season opener or within the first couple weeks of the season which would allow him to avoid the minimum four-week absence that comes with an IR stint. Head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed to reporters Lowe was an IR candidate at final cuts. He may still be one now that he's on the team.

It's unclear exactly how severe Height's ankle injury is. There's a chance he's ready to go for the season opener, but given that he missed the 49ers' preseason finale it's worth wondering whether the team will shut him down for the first few weeks to ensure he's fully healthy when he does return. Keep an eye on his participation in the three days leading up to the team's departure for Australia.

Gifford has been dealing with a hamstring injury since early in training camp. Those injuries can be tricky to deal with and it wouldn't be a surprise if the 49ers determine some additional time off would be helpful for the special teams ace. With seven linebackers on the roster it would make sense that at least one is headed for an injured list.

Put Martin in the same boat as Gifford, although he suffered his injury in the second preseason game. That puts him on a different timeline than Gifford. The severity of the injuries will matter here, but with a logjam at LB Martin could be on his way to IR.

It was a rough camp for Hobbs who had a real shot to carve out a role. He came back from one injury and quickly hurt his groin and hasn't practiced since early in camp. Given his lack of practice time he's a prime IR candidate who may or may not ever get the return designation.

Prysock hurt his shoulder in the preseason finale and Shanahan said he was a candidate to go on IR. Perhaps additional testing over the last few days showed he won't need to be out an extended period. An injury late in the preseason could be tough from a timeline standpoint, though, and Prysock may head to IR if the team determines he needs more than a week or two to get right.

It would appear Mustapha is trending toward a return since he made the initial roster and hasn't participated since the early days of camp. Hamstrings are tricky, though, and he's a potential starter once he's healthy. The 49ers won't likely want to rush him back into action.
